articles.title: A.J. Brown says he's not 100 percent after returning from high-ankle sprain: 'I'm pushing through'
articles.summary: A.J. Brown missed multiple games this season due to a high-ankle sprain.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown was supposed to be the key to unlocking an even stronger offense in 2026. While an early injury scuttled those plans, Brown was able to return to action in Week 6. So far, though, he hasn't looked like himself.

In two games since he's been back, Brown has been targeted 16 times, but has hauled in just six of those balls for 75 yards. He's also fumbled once since his return. That production is far below what the Patriots expected when the team gave up a first-round pick for the wideout.

Turns out, there's a reason for that. Though Brown is back, he's still battling through the after effects of his high-ankle sprain. The 29-year-old admitted as much Wednesday, telling Boston Sports Journal he's " pushing through " it right now.

When asked whether he was still trying to regain his explosiveness after the injury, Brown said:

"Yeah, sometimes, you know, I see it, and sometimes, I'm pushing through," he admitted. "But none of that stuff even matters. I'm out here, so I'm going."

Despite that, the Patriots haven't limited Brown's playing time since he's been back. The wideout played 76 percent of the team's offensive snaps in Week 6 and 91 percent of the team's offensive snaps in Week 7.

Injuries have certainly played a role in that decision, as the team is without Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins at the moment.

Those injuries make it hard to project when Brown will feel completely back to normal. The Patriots do have a bye in Week 11, giving Brown at least another week in the season to rest the injury, though it's unclear if that will be enough.

When healthy, Brown has proven to be one of the best receivers in the game. Despite missing a few games in both 2024 and 2025, he still managed to exceed 1,000 receiving yards in each season.

That streak could be put to the test in 2026, though. In the three games he's played, Brown has just 101 total yards. He would need some massive performances moving forward to get to 1,000 yards on the season, a much tougher task if Brown is still dealing with his high-ankle sprain.

Ultimately, the Patriots don't necessarily need that level of performance out of Brown during the regular season. If the star receiver is fully healthy for the playoffs, that's all that matters as they look to bounce back after last season's Super Bowl loss.

articles.title: Did Bears overpay for Jeffery Simmons? What recent DL trades from Cowboys, Rams, Packers might teach
articles.summary: Initial reaction from NFL executives, talent evaluators and coaches questioned the price the Bears paid to poach Simmons, even if his talents are undeniable.
articles.body:
In the short term, the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions should shudder.

Kyler Murray, Jordan Love and Jared Goff's lives just got harder.

Offensive success against the Chicago Bears won't come as easily after Thursday morning. Good luck to the NFC North quarterbacks.

The Chicago Bears and Tennessee Titans agreed to a trade for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , according to multiple reports. The Bears sent their 2027 first-round pick, 2028 first-round pick and 2027 fourth-round pick to Tennessee in exchange for Simmons and the Titans' 2028 fifth, per the Titans.

Simmons immediately upgrades a managing-but-inefficient defense. Through seven games in Tennessee this year, he registered four sacks, a forced fumble and fumble recovery, 13 pressures, nine quarterback hits and 38 tackles. No defensive tackle has won his pass-rush reps more than Simmons' 27% clip, per ESPN's pass-rush win rate metric . Simmons was that efficient even as he played high-volume snaps, pass-rushing 124 times in seven games while facing double teams on 84% of snaps, per ESPN.

The Bears' top player on that list before Thursday was Grady Jarrett, who ranked 18th with a 16% win rate.

So no one's doubting that the Bears are better now, better this season and better in 2027 as they acquire Simmons. But initial reaction from executives, talent evaluators and coaches across the league questioned the price the Bears paid to poach Simmons .

"Great trade value-wise [for Tennessee] long term," one AFC assistant coach told Yahoo Sports.

An NFC executive deemed the price "a lot" when an executive from a second AFC team said they congratulated Titans counterparts on the return.

What would executives and talent evaluators from other teams pay for Simmons?

One NFC executive valued Simmons as worth a first- and a second-round pick. An AFC executive said Simmons is indeed "very, very good" and thus would warrant "maybe a one and change." An executive from another NFC team noted value differs based on a team's current needs at the position, but for the Bears, they'd consider a 2027 first and 2028 third worth acquiring him. (Teams differ on whether they view the value of picks consistent across years or whether they discount the value of a later-year pick due to the limited ability to gain value from the asset in the interim.)

So will trading two firsts and change prove worthwhile for the Bears? A look at recent blockbuster defensive line trades call that into question.

How Micah Parsons, Myles Garrett, Quinnen Williams have impacted their teams so far

There is always the risk of injury for any player acquisition. Teams calculate cost-benefit analyses by the player, often considering past injuries and age as the top predictor of future injuries.

So the Green Bay Packers' 2025 trade for Micah Parsons and the Los Angeles Rams' 2026 trade for Myles Garrett are so far more unlucky than they were reckless. But each can serve as a cautionary tale.

The Packers sent their 2026 first-round pick, 2027 first-round pick and defensive tackle Kenny Clark to the Dallas Cowboys in August 2025 in exchange for Parsons, who had earned four Pro Bowl berths and two first-team All-Pro nods in his four Dallas years. Parsons was productive in 14 games last season, collecting 12.5 sacks, 41 tackles and two forced fumbles. Then he tore his ACL on Dec. 14. He has yet to return to practice.

The Rams sent a 2027 first-round pick, 2028 second-round pick, 2029 third-round pick and edge rusher Jared Verse to the Cleveland Browns on June 1 in exchange for Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year.

Garrett played 40 snaps in LA's season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers but clearly was not himself. The Rams explained later that swelling in Garrett's knee was too intense to play through productively, and he would require surgery. Seven weeks later, Garrett has yet to return to practice .

Does that mean each trade is destined to be a bust? No. But the losses incurred while Parsons and Garrett have been sidelined impact not only the value of the payday their teams are contributing but also the value of the draft picks sent away. The Rams expected their 2027 first-round pick would be in the late 20s at the highest and hoped it was pick No. 32. They surprised the league by selecting quarterback Ty Simpson in the 2026 first round in part because they didn't anticipate a 2027 first being within range of a quarterback. Eleven weeks remain in the regular season. But the Rams currently sit at 3-4, which means the Browns are projected for the 14th overall pick, per Tankathon.com . At 4-3, the Packers' 2027 first currently pegs the Cowboys to select 20th.

"It's hard to bank that far out in advance," an NFC executive said of teams hoping their traded-away firsts will arrive late in the round.

The Cowboys' trade-deadline acquisition of Quinnen Williams a year ago in some ways has proven even less successful. Williams has provided defensive leadership and stayed healthy. But the Cowboys' defense has struggled even with him on the field.

Sure, they're better with him: Since the beginning of 2025, the Cowboys' defense has allowed 356.9 total yards per game with Williams compared to 402.9 without him, per TruMedia Sports. He's helped them down from 143.9 to 122.5 rushing yards per game, 259 to 234.4 passing yards (he has not been the only variable during the that period). But even at 376 yards per game, the Cowboys rank second-worst in the league in yards allowed across 2025-2026, and they're third worst this year alone. The Cowboys have allowed more points this season than all but the New Orleans Saints, Las Vegas Raiders and Arizona Cardinals — rebuilding teams. Across the two seasons, only the Cardinals are leakier.

Will Simmons buck the recent trends and meaningfully improve the Bears?

"He's a really good player," an NFC executive said. "Definitely makes them better immediately."

Why elite DTs like Simmons 'disarm' offenses in a way edge rushers don't

The reality: If the Bears win the Super Bowl, advance to the Super Bowl or perhaps even advance to a conference championship with a heavily contributing Simmons, no one will care about the future picks that may or may not have panned out.

Another reality: Even when considering the recent heavy-hitting defensive line trades, this move remains unprecedented. Simmons is the first defensive tackle in the common draft era (since 1967) to be traded for multiple first-round picks, per ESPN Research .

If healthy, he can help the 5-2 Bears catch 6-0 Minnesota. He can help a defense that has benefited greatly from staying off the field (the Bears lead the league with a 35:30 average time of possession) while struggling on a per-play basis. Chicago ranks eighth in yards allowed per game (313.4) but last in yards allowed per play (6.25). No team has allowed more pass yards per play than the Bears defense's 8.15.

Edge rushers remain a vaunted bunch in the NFL. But elite pass-rushing defensive tackles are frustrating offensive coordinators and quarterbacks at rising rates.

"It's not like he's the right defensive end that you can choose to run away from or always help to — it's really hard to build help elements into a game plan for a nose tackle," Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher told Yahoo Sports during training camp. "It's just not something you're used to doing and your flexibility and how you do it is not nearly as great as when you start talking about trying to help edge players and guys of that nature. There's only so much you can do."

Acquiring and developing interior offensive linemen, as the Seattle Seahawks (ironically the Bears' next opponent) just did with Quenton Nelson , helps. But without the top-shelf talent, offenses struggle against teams with top defensive tackles.

"It just disarms you because I don't know what you do to counteract that other than you just really focus on the technique of this interior line and you've got to be really cognizant of what types of schemes you're trying to run and how often that guy's truly one-on-one," Pitcher said.

"So if he's able to create pocket push or penetration, it's right there in your lap. And when an end creates penetration, hopefully you're firm enough inside that you can step up and climb escape lanes. When that [defensive tackle] is in your face, your escape lanes are out. That's never a good thing. Running sideways and backwards at quarterback in the NFL is a good way to not play very long.

Consider that, and one NFC talent evaluator deeming Simmons "MUCH better" than Williams — "not even in the same category" — and the Bears' price suddenly looks less wild if still steep.

The ceiling for Chicago's newest acquisition is high. How close will Simmons come to reaching it?

articles.title: ‘No Shame, No Guilt,’ ‘He’s Disgusting’ — NFL Fans Rip Packers RB Josh Jacobs for Apparent Handcuffs Celebration After TD vs. Panthers
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs returned to the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 after missing the first six games of the 2026 season while on the NFL’s Commissioner’s Exempt List fo...
articles.body:
Josh Jacobs returned to the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 after missing the first six games of the 2026 season while on the NFL's Commissioner's Exempt List following his May arrest in a domestic dispute. But two weeks into his return, fans were aghast at one particular display from the three-time Pro Bowler.

After scoring a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football, Jacobs did a celebration in the end zone that seemed to look like him walking with handcuffs, with his hands tied behind his back. Given the severity of the lawsuit, fans were infuriated by his gesture.

A domestic dispute in May 2026 led to his arrest. Initially facing five counts of battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct, strangulation and suffocation, as well as intimidation of a victim, he was formally charged with battery and criminal damage to property.

Pleading no contest to both charges, he was placed on one year of supervision, alongside restitution, a fine, and a no-contact order. It also led to him missing the first six games of the season, before returning in Week 7.

But in Week 8, things took an ugly turn. After scoring a second-quarter touchdown, Jacobs performed a celebration that some social media users interpreted as mimicking someone being handcuffed. The gesture immediately drew criticism given his recent legal case.

Speaking after the game, the Packers star alleged that the broadcast did not show the full celebration. "It was more to it than that," Jacobs said. "They stopped showing the celebration after that. Like I said, it is what it is." Jacobs added that he was instead modeling his celebration after a gospel song called "Break Every Chain."

"The guys did it with me," Jacobs said. "I didn't think it was going to be something that could be perceived a certain type of way. But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

The official account of the "Pardon My Take" podcast wondered , "Did Josh Jacobs just hit a Handcuff Celebration?"

One fan was shocked at the way the NFL was handling the situation, writing, "Yes, remember when players used to get punished for committing crimes like Ray Rice."

Another believed it was a problem unique to sports and just one other role, as he argued, "He's disgusting. I hate that professional sports is the one profession where this type of behaviour doesn't end in termination."

For one fan, it was a clear double standard from the NFL, as he claimed, "The NFL will allow Josh Jacobs to play and then try to lecture the public about social issues."

Another fan didn't mince words as he exclaimed, "Embarrassing that you're allowing him to play," tagging both the NFL and the NFL Commissioner's account.

As one fan rhetorically asked , "Is Josh Jacobs not the most disgusting human right now?" another fan mocked , "He'll probably sue to keep this video hidden, too."

It remains to be seen if the league takes further action against Jacobs for his display. But given the sensitivity around the issue, there will be more than a few calls from fans for the league to look into the matter.

articles.title: New monster in the Midway: Why Jeffery Simmons could be worth the price for Bears in a wide-open NFL
articles.summary: Simmons is a one-man game-wrecker on every down and in every situation, which will give a needed lift to a Chicago defense that has been punching above its w...
articles.body:
The NFL, the most parity-driven major sports league, feels even more wide open this year. Even the perceived powerhouses entering the season and teams with the best records have flaws that are already being picked at by opponents.

Betting markets and bettors are keeping plenty of teams alive. As of Thursday evening, FanDuel had 11 NFC teams with +164 or shorter odds to make the playoffs, and seven teams with +1100 odds or shorter to win the Super Bowl. Thirteen teams were at +2500 or shorter to hoist the Lombardi Trophy in February.

This open competition leads to opportunity. And opportunity leads to action. Even when the Nov. 10 trade deadline was still a ways away, teams started to address their weaknesses. The Dallas Cowboys added Joey Porter Jr., the Baltimore Ravens nabbed Cam Jurgens. Now with the deadline growing closer , NFL teams have decided to strike. First, Quenton Nelson was shipped off to the Seattle Seahawks from the sinking ship known as the Indianapolis Colts. Soon after, DeForest Buckner returned to the San Francisco 49ers to bolster their defensive front.

Then, on Thursday, the Chicago Bears fired a shot across the bow to the rest of the NFC and NFL, trading two future first-round draft picks and a fourth-rounder to the Tennessee Titans for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round selection .

Now that's some real action for a trade deadline!

In an escalating arms race, the Bears added one of the premier players in the NFL, defense or otherwise. Before the deal, Simmons had played in Tennessee his entire seven-plus year career for a franchise that hasn't been in a prime-time game since 2024. Yet, he still managed to rack up postseason accolades for his work in the trenches, nabbing a first-team All-Pro in 2025, two second-team nods and four Pro Bowls. Simmons might not have received a ton of Defensive Player of the Year chatter, but his name was always on the short list over the past few seasons, at least in this writer's opinion. He turned 29 this summer, safely considered within his athletic prime, and plays a position that has a smoother aging curve than other spots that might rely on more quick-twitch athleticism than defensive tackle, where brawn can help stave off regression. There were 17 defensive tackles who played 400 or more snaps in 2025 who were 30 or older, compared to 18 for all other defensive positions combined , according to The Athletic's Paul Dehner Jr.

Other models have shown a similar aging pattern for defensive tackles, which makes sense because of the prerequisites for playing the position. Offensive guard is similar on the other side of the ball. As are other power and strength-focused athletes like heavyweights in combat sports and first basemen in baseball, for example.

Simmons is under contract until his age-33 season on what should be a deal that ages well, especially if the salary cap continues to rise. The Bears are giving up two first-rounders, a rich asking price , but also more justifiable considering the player they acquired and the position that he plays. The draft picks also reset right as Caleb Williams' potential new deal (it's really as likely as can be at this point) should kick in, when a need for cheaper talent becomes more valued as his salary cap hit multiplies several times over.

But enough about future problems and conundrums. Let's get to the fireworks factory! What does Jeffery Simmons bring to Chicago? To make this as Chicago-y as possible: a monster is back in the Midway.

If the accolades didn't already speak to Simmons' ability, the eye test quickly does. Simmons, already hard to miss at 6-foot-4, 300-plus pounds and with the bright red sleeves he wears under his pads, quickly made an impression when he manned the middle of Tennessee's defense over the past few seasons.

Simmons brings it on every snap. He's a mauler in every sense of the word. Even when playing for a team that hasn't been competing for much, Simmons made the most of his chances in one-on-one opportunities, particularly on obvious pass situations, and created big plays against double-teams (including in the run game).

Simmons currently leads all defensive tackles in pressures this season, per Next Gen Stats, with four sacks to boot. He has 10 pressures when double-teamed this season, and the highest pressure rate when double-teamed as well; three of his sacks have come when double-teamed.

Since 2024, Simmons has racked up the second-most pressures and an 11.7% pressure rate, which ranks fifth among all qualifying defensive tackles. Of his 137 pressures over that time period, 36 have come when double-teamed, too. He ranks second in quick pressure rate as well, which is extremely impactful since defensive tackles have the shortest path to the quarterback, and thus can impact a pass play even when they don't come down with a sack (don't worry, Simmons' 20 sacks since 2024 ranks second as well).

Again, Simmons is a mauler , not a gap-shooter who quickly wins but can get washed out of plays or can't hold up against double-teams on the inside. Simmons is a dominant force against the run as well.

Simmons has 31 tackles this year against the run and 21 run stops, which are tackles that lead to unsuccessful gains (in terms of success rate) for the offense. Both of those marks rank second this season. Since 2024, Simmons leads all defensive tackles in run tackles with 143 and 105 stops. That's an absurd number, especially paired with Simmons' pass-rush ability. These aren't empty calorie jumps on the pile when a running back is already gaining a first down. Simmons is not only disrupting offenses on every down, he shuts the door on them to begin with. His run stops have generated -69 EPA since 2024, which ranks second behind only Colts defensive tackle Grover Stewart (teams in need of run defense should be calling about him).

Simmons is a one-man game-wrecker on every down and in every situation. It's something not a lot of defensive linemen can do, especially as teams have leaned into using space-eaters on early downs and kicking edge rushers inside on passing downs.

Pointing out what Simmons does every down is important here. Because while the Bears' offense is starting to roll again with Williams healthy and Ben Johnson calling plays, their defense has been punching above its weight this season. Their game plans this season (and last year, for that matter) under defensive coordinator Dennis Allen have been essentially "let's survive until third down and then give them the crazy fists."

The Bears don't have a ton of aces on their front to get after the passer (unless you count slot dynamo Kyler Gordon). Austin Booker has flashes but with Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve, not a single defensive lineman or edge has a pressure rate even above 9% other than Grady Jarrett at 9.9% (for reference, league average is currently at 10.8%). To make up for this lack of pass rush juice, Allen uses his deep rolodex of pressure goofiness that he likes to throw at offenses on passing downs that are supremely effective.

Overall, the Bears rank 12th in EPA per play and have some strong success rate numbers (ranking third overall, 10th against running back runs, and fourth against the pass). The problem, which might not be a problem now but when facing the better offenses in the playoffs, is that those numbers are buoyed by their 26.1% third-down conversion rate allowed, which ranks first in the NFL.

When you shine a light on the early-down splits for this defense, the warts and blemishes start to show: the Bears rank 32nd in EPA per play on early downs and allow the most yards per play (6.8) and net yards per attempt (9.3! NINE POINT THREE!). Their success rates drop to the middle of the pack (16th overall, 15th against the pass, 13th against the run) and their sack rates and pressure rates drop from third and sixth, respectively, to ninth and 13th.

Again, not a real problem right now and a credit to Allen and the Bears' defense for making the most of what they are, but the Bears have currently played the 30th-ranked offensive schedule so far this season, per FTN. A defense that ranks 30th in explosive passes allowed and 21st in explosive designed runs allowed (and 29th in yards before contact on running back runs) is just asking to get their nose bloodied, or their head taken straight off, against the better offenses the rest of the season and when the weather gets colder.

The strength of this Bears team is their explosive offense that can run and throw the ball equally well, especially with a now-healthy Williams firing Hadouken -like passes all over the field to his deep group of pass-catchers. Their defense, while well-coached, still needed reinforcements. Simmons is not only a few more munitions of ammo, he's a bomb for Allen to ride like the Major in Dr. Strangelove.

The Bears are betting on Simmons to help them win on first and second downs so they can let Allen unleash his wickedness on third and fourth downs. That will allow them to win every down with the threat of chaos always about to be unleashed by their defensive play-caller, a combination that is so important to have come playoff time. Get off the field and get the ball back in the hands of their dynamic quarterback and explosive offense, creating runs on opponents like a trapping basketball team stealing the ball and launching another 3 before the opposition can even catch its breath. A sprinkling, nay a pouring, of venom and spice to make everything nice in Chicago.

General manager Ryan Poles, Johnson and the Bears are pushing it in a wide-open season and making it a spooky season for other teams in the NFC.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes’ kids steal the Halloween spotlight with pumpkin heads in adorable family snap
articles.summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes took their three kids to a pumpkin patch this week, and Brittany shared the day on Instagram Stories on Wednesday, Oct. 28.
articles.body: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes took their three kids to a pumpkin patch this week, and Brittany shared the day on Instagram Stories on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Sterling, 5, Bronze, 3, and Golden, 21 months, posed on hay bales and sat on carousel animals with their dad. Not every photo came out sharp, and Brittany said so herself. The outing follows an Oct. 14 press conference where the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback admitted he had forgotten Halloween until his wife asked about costumes. Patrick and Brittany are both 31, and the season is in full swing.Mahomes family spends Wednesday at the pumpkin patchBrittany, a former soccer player, posted several Stories from the outing. The first was a slightly blurry shot of the kids on a haystack among pumpkins. She wrote over it, “Out with the clear pictures,” and added a crying laughing emoji. Anyone who has tried to photograph three young children at once will understand.The other pictures were sharper. Sterling grinned from a flamingo on a carousel. Patrick stood between Bronze and Golden, who smiled from their own animals on the ride. A final shot showed Sterling posing on top of bear statues, with lights glowing in the trees behind her.Patrick forgot about Halloween until Brittany askedPatrick had other things on his mind when Halloween came up on Oct. 14. Season routines had pushed the holiday out of his head, he told reporters at a press conference.“Once you get in season, you’re focused on that week. You focus on that week, then you try to win that week and then you move on to the next week,” the Chiefs athlete said. “It surprised me. I forgot about Halloween.”Brittany was the one who brought it up. “Brittany asked me, ‘What are we going to be for Halloween?’ I’m like, ‘I didn’t even think about that,’ ” he admitted.A reporter asked what the family would wear. “I can’t tell now,” Patrick replied. “There’s options because you never know with kids. So we have multiple options. I don’t even know yet. I still have a couple of options.”Brittany keeps sharing the fall seasonBrittany has been posting fall content for weeks. On Oct. 3, she shared photos from Johnson Farms Plants and Pumpkins with the caption “It’s fall yall🍂” The kids met animals, picked apples and did arts and crafts. Other pictures showed the family together and posing with mascots.Football has been part of the routine too. She posted shots of herself and the kids cheering on Patrick at a Chiefs game, captioned “The best times🥹❤️,” on Oct. 21. Back on Aug. 4, the family watched training camp at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, Mo., as Patrick reported for his 10th NFL season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A Tom Brady romance, a ‘Backstabber’ accusation and 15 years of friendship: Inside the supermodel fallout
articles.summary: Tom Brady’s reported romance with Victoria’s Secret model Candice Swanepoel has sparked speculation about a bitter split between Swanepoel and her
articles.body: Tom Brady’s reported romance with Victoria’s Secret model Candice Swanepoel has sparked speculation about a bitter split between Swanepoel and her longtime friend Joan Smalls. According to reports, Smalls and Brady were romantically involved on and off for about a year, making the latest relationship rumors especially sensitive given the models’ 15-year friendship. Alleged social media comments accusing an unnamed person of betrayal have added to the attention, though neither model has publicly confirmed the full story. For now, the reported fallout remains a mix of insider claims, cryptic posts and unanswered questions.Joan Smalls’ ‘Backstabber’ comments put her friendship with Candice Swanepoel under scrutinyThe reported rift became a talking point after Smalls allegedly responded to a fan asking about her friendship with Swanepoel. In comments that were later deleted, she reportedly wrote, “I'm not friends with backstabbers.” Another message appeared to explain her frustration, referring to broken trust and a lack of respect after years of friendship."And the disrespect and carelessness in how they treat you is so unimaginable. There’s no going back. Some people lack humility and moral compass," she reportedly wrote."And the way they gaslight, lie and minimize your feelings is the worst slap in the face after 15yrs of friendship. Not a sorry said or written. Onwards and upwards!!!"The timing fueled speculation. Both models attended the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show, but fans noticed they were not seen together as they had been in the past. Reports also linked their apparent distance to Brady, with sources claiming Smalls felt blindsided by her friend's reported relationship with the retired quarterback.Still, the distinction between reported claims and confirmed facts matters. Neither model has publicly laid out the full reason for the apparent tension, and Brady has not confirmed a relationship with Swanepoel. The online comments may offer clues about hurt feelings, but they do not establish exactly what happened between the longtime friends.Candice Swanepoel’s response leaves the door open on a 15-year friendshipSwanepoel's representative offered a measured response when asked about the reports, stressing the model's preference for privacy rather than addressing the alleged romantic dispute directly."Candice has always been exceptionally private about her personal life, with her focus remaining on raising her children. She and Joan share a longstanding history and a friendship that Candice will always respect."That statement neither confirms a feud nor dismisses the history between the two models. Their friendship stretches back roughly 15 years, through careers that have often placed them in the same fashion circles and major industry events. A dispute involving a reported romance would therefore carry a different weight from an ordinary celebrity dating rumor.Brady, meanwhile, has been linked to several women since finalizing his divorce from Gisele Bündchen in October 2022. His reported connection with Swanepoel has now brought attention to a personal situation involving two established figures in the modeling world.For now, the biggest unanswered question is not whether Brady and Swanepoel are dating, but whether a friendship that lasted 15 years can withstand the reported breach of trust. Until the people involved speak more clearly, the claims should remain just that: reports, not a settled account of what ended the relationship between two longtime friends.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft Big Board: 6 QBs Rank Among Top 50 Overall Prospects
articles.summary: With the college football season past the halfway point, here are Rob Rang's 50 best prospects in the 2027 NFL Draft.
articles.body: The hope at the beginning of every college football season is that good players will improve to become great and that previously undiscovered talent will make a draft class that much better. The reality, however, is that some players regress. And with today’s liberal transfer policy and the allure of NIL dollars, players are more hesitant than ever to enter the NFL before exhausting their college eligibility. We won’t know for certain which prospects will make up the Class of 2027 until mid-January. But if the 2027 NFL Draft were to take place tomorrow, here is how I would rank the top prospects. 50. Lance Heard, OTKentucky Wildcats NFL Player Comp: Tytus Howard, Browns Size, power and positional versatility are awfully important boxes to check when evaluating offensive tackles, and Heard possesses all of those. At 6-foot-5, 325 pounds, with vines for arms and experience playing both right and left tackle following tours at Tennessee and LSU, Heard has the frame and game that scream NFL starter. 49. Damon Wilson II, DEMiami Hurricanes NFL Player Comp: K’Lavon Chaisson, Commanders NFL teams are hesitant to invest early picks in specialists, but Wilson offers one of the best combinations of burst and bend of this year’s edge rushers. Teams will pry into his reasons for transferring from Georgia to Missouri to Miami over the past three seasons but his production at every stop is undeniable. 48. Devon Jackson, LBOregon Ducks NFL Player Comp: Quay Walker, Raiders Say what you will about Oregon’s collective struggles this season, their individual talent will be recognized by the NFL soon enough. A runaway freight train with true knockdown power, Jackson is blessed with an exceptional combination of size and speed and will be one of this year’s flashiest at the Scouting Combine. 47. Deuce Alexander, WROle Miss Rebels NFL Player Comp: Jaylen Waddle, Broncos The 5-foot-11, 180-pound Alexander is significantly slighter than most of the other receivers on my Big Board and has more drops in traffic than I’d prefer. He is lightning fast, however, offering the breakaway element every NFL team is looking for in a deep threat. 46. Ryan Coleman-Williams, WRAlabama Crimson Tide NFL Player Comp: DeVonta Smith, Eagles Durability and drops are concerns, but the flashes with Coleman-Williams are so bright that I had to include him on my list. He’s a proven playmaker, averaging 16.4 yards per catch with 18 touchdowns in two and a half seasons of SEC football. He also won’t turn 20 until February. 45. Matayo Uiagalelei, DEOregon Ducks NFL Player Comp: Bradley Chubb, Bills It has become an annual tradition: I find a pass-rusher I seem to be higher on than my peers. A year ago, it was Gabe Jacas. In 2024, it was Nic Scourton. Uiagalelei has size, agility, power, instincts and eye-popping production. Oh, and he’s just 21 years old. What’s not to like? 44. Sammy Omosigho, LBUCLA Bruins NFL Player Comp: Mack Wilson, Cardinals Highlighted a few weeks ago as one of the fastest rising players in this class, Omosigho personifies an unbeaten UCLA squad meriting more attention. The Oklahoma transfer is a runaway freight train as a hitter, generating rare explosive power with a knack for producing fumbles. 43. Bear Alexander, DEOregon Ducks NFL Player Comp: Alim McNeil, Lions A double transfer who also spent time at Georgia and USC, Alexander lives up to his nickname, using an exciting blend of initial quickness and long-armed power to rag-doll would-be blockers. His tape features more lapses than I’d prefer, but the talent is there. 42. Carter Smith, OLIndiana Hoosiers NFL Player Comp: Kevin Zeitler, Packers Smith has played a critical role on the blindside for the defending national champion Hoosiers, but he lacks ideal arm length and has the orneriness and physicality that project really well inside at guard. He is an iron man, having started the past 49 consecutive games (and all of them at left tackle). 41. KJ Bolden, SGeorgia Bulldogs NFL Player Comp: Malik Mustafa, 49ers He’ll take risky angles in pursuit, but teams looking for a safety who can run the alley and generate collisions like a linebacker will love Bolden, a three-year starter with excellent speed and proven ball skills. 40. Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, LBNotre Dame Fighting Irish NFL Player Comp: Frankie Luvu, Commanders Viliamu-Asa isn’t the most technically sound defender in this class, but he might just be the most violent, which is an excellent baseline for an NFL linebacker. He is a heat-seeking missile who seems to thrive on contact. 39. Niki Prongos, OTStanford Cardinal NFL Player Comp: Kolton Miller, Raiders At a solid 6-foot-7, 310 pounds, with broad shoulders and a trim middle, Prongos looks the part of a modern NFL tackle. He’s quick, powerful and versatile, having started at guard and right tackle for UCLA prior to transferring to Stanford. His best football may still be ahead, considering he didn't begin playing football until his senior year of high school. 38. Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace, DEKentucky Wildcats NFL Player Comp: Jermaine Johnson, Titans An FCS transfer from South Dakota with 14.5 tackles for loss and 8.5 sacks over a season and a half in the SEC, Humphrey-Grace is a name to learn. He is surprisingly nimble at 6-foot-4, 271 pounds, and he uses his length and strength well as a bull rusher. 37. Cayden Green, OLMissouri Tigers NFL Player Comp: Robert Hunt, Panthers Green stars at left tackle for the Tigers, but I like his burly frame and power better inside at guard, where he started 13 games as a true freshman for Oklahoma back in 2024. While he’ll need to learn to play with better knee bend and keep his legs driving through contact, I see a future longtime starter. 36. Devan Thompkins, DEAlabama Crimson Tide NFL Player Comp: Keion White, 49ers A USC transfer some once compared to former Trojan Leonard Williams, Thompkins’ calling cards are his unique blend of size (6-foot-5, 300 pounds) and versatility. Alabama lines him up all over the defensive line and even as a stand-up rusher. As you’d expect with his size, Thompkins is powerful, but he’s also quite agile. 35. Will Echoles, DTOle Miss Rebels NFL Player Comp: Milton Williams, Patriots Echoles has struggled to live up to expectations so far this season, generating just 21 tackles, including four for loss and 1.5 sacks over the first seven games of the year after posting 68 stops, 11.5 TFL and five sacks a year ago. He’s quicker than his square-ish frame suggests and pairs his hands and feet well, but he needs to ramp up the production if he hopes to earn a high grade from the NFL’s Advisory Committee. 34. Cam Coleman, WRTexas Longhorns NFL Player Comp: Quentin Johnston, Chargers Coleman looks the part of a future NFL star, teasing with a rare combination of size (6-foot-3, 200 pounds), acceleration and body control. There are some concerning peaks and valleys to his game, however, with ugly drops against Oklahoma and Mississippi raising questions about his concentration. 33. Jaylen McClain, SOhio State Buckeyes NFL Player Comp: Budda Baker, Cardinals With Caleb Downs now a member of the Dallas Cowboys, I expected there to be a fairly dramatic drop-off for the Buckeyes at the safety position. Instead, McClain has emerged as a legitimate playmaker in his own right while also emerging as one of the nation’s surest open-field tacklers. 32. Trevor Goosby, OTTexas Longhorns NFL Player Comp: Rashawn Slater, Chargers Viewed as a possible top-10 pick prior to the season, Goosby suffered a season-ending knee injury against Mississippi last weekend. He’s a gifted pass blocker when healthy but had extensive medical concerns even prior to this injury, including open-heart surgery in high school. Whenever he chooses to enter the NFL, his medical evaluation will ultimately determine where he’ll be drafted. His talent is undeniable. 31. Darian Mensah, QBMiami Hurricanes NFL Player Comp: Jared Goff, Lions With an FBS-best 81.4% completion rate, 22 touchdown passes and just one interception so far this season, Mensah is my midseason pick to win the Heisman Trophy. He relies more on anticipation than arm strength on outbreaking routes, however, and could struggle to duplicate this success in the NFL. 30. Jamari Johnson, TEOregon Ducks NFL Player Comp: Tucker Kraft, Packers Like a lot of the Ducks, this season has not gone as well as expected for Johnson, but scouts will look past the middling production and recognize his upside. The transfer from Louisville offers an exciting combination of size (6-foot-5, 257 pounds), agility and soft hands that should translate into greater success in the NFL than he’s ever had at the collegiate level. 29. Kewan Lacy, RBOle Miss Rebels NFL Player Comp: De'Von Achane, Dolphins After leading the country with 335 touches a year ago, the 5-foot-11, 205-pound Lacy has struggled with nagging injuries this season. When healthy, he’s truly dynamic, pairing vision with elusiveness, speed and underrated leg drive. 28. Will Heldt, DEClemson Tigers NFL Player Comp: Josh Hines-Allen, Jaguars He isn’t the twitchiest edge rusher of this class, but the 6-foot-5, 260-pound Heldt’s length, strength and tenacity stand out against the run and the pass. He anticipates the snap count well and is surprisingly effective in chasing down ballcarriers from behind, showing great hand-eye coordination to trip up opponents seemingly out of his grasp. 27. Princewill Umanmielen, DELSU Tigers NFL Player Comp: Nik Bonitto, Broncos The NFL is willing to pay a premium for speed rushers, and Umanmielen is among the best in this class, generating 17.5 sacks over his past 23 games. He is a legitimate QB stalker with the initial burst and lateral agility to make tackles look silly trying to corral him. 26. Kelley Jones, DBMississippi State Bulldogs NFL Player Comp: Joey Porter Jr., Cowboys Jones will have plenty of doubters because there just aren’t many 6-foot-4 cornerbacks in the NFL, but four years of impressive tape in the SEC doesn’t lie. Like any long-levered defensive back, Jones can’t change direction quite as fluidly as some of the shorter corners, but his long arms crowd receivers at the stem and the catch point and his lengthy strides allow him to accelerate in a flash. 25. Yhonzae Pierre, DEAlabama Crimson Tide NFL Player Comp: Derick Hall, Seahawks Edge rushers selected in the first round typically have great twitch and bend. Pierre’s game, on the other hand, is power, which he uses to violently beat blockers to impact the run and pass. 24. Boubacar Traore, DENotre Dame Fighting Irish NFL Player Comp: Laiatu Latu, Colts Complementing his burst and power, Traore is among the more polished edge rushers of this class, incorporating Euro steps and compact spins to leave pass blockers in his wake. He is a big-play magnet with 21.5 tackles for loss and 14 sacks over his college career, as well as five forced fumbles, two interceptions and two TD returns. 23. Trey'Dez Green, TELSU Tigers NFL Player Comp: Kyle Pitts, Falcons A knee sprain kept Green out for four games earlier this season, so the lack of production (19 catches for 272 yards and two touchdowns) has allowed him to fly somewhat under the radar. When healthy, the 6-foot-6, 237-pounder is a proven mismatch who projects as a dynamic weapon in the NFL. 22. A'Mauri Washington, DTOregon Ducks NFL Player Comp: Kenneth Grant, Dolphins With just half a tackle for loss in seven games this season, some analysts won’t be as high on Washington as NFL teams will. The 6-foot-3, 330-pounder’s value lies with his rare combination of initial quickness and girth. Critics who suggest that he doesn’t impact the passing game fail to recognize his 15 (and counting) career pass breakups, proving his ability to collapse the pocket. 21. Xavier Gilliam, DTTennessee Volunteers NFL Player Comp: Nnamdi Madubuike, Ravens One of this year’s flashiest breakout stars, Gilliam might have the quickest first step of any DT in the country. He explodes off the ball, wrecking plays with penetration. With 11.5 tackles for loss (including six sacks) so far this season for the Vols, Gilliam has nearly as many stops behind the line of scrimmage as he had total tackles (16) during his first two years at Penn State. 20. Jordan Seaton, OTLSU Tigers NFL Player Comp: Olu Fashanu, Jets A consensus five-star recruit from IMG Academy who started the first 22 games of his college career at Colorado, Seaton has all the traits to eventually become a premium left tackle, including initial quickness, balance and size. He’s 21-years old and while he hasn’t surrendered a sack this season, he needs to get stronger and polish up his technique before making the NFL leap. His upside, however, warrants a first-round investment. 19. Jadan Baugh, RBFlorida Gators NFL Player Comp: Jonathan Taylor, Colts At nearly 6-foot-1, 225 pounds, Baugh looks like your traditional downhill runner. But he complements his power with impressive elusiveness and breakaway speed. Baugh is a bit of a throwback as a true workhorse. 18. CJ Carr, QBNotre Dame Fighting Irish NFL Player Comp: Kirk Cousins, Raiders It has been 20 years since the last Notre Dame quarterback (Brady Quinn) was selected in the first round. Smart, poised and an accurate deep ball passer, Carr has a chance to end that streak for the Irish. 17. Kade Pieper, CIowa Hawkeyes NFL Player Comp: Tyler Linderbaum, Raiders Pieper plays right guard for the Hawkeyes but projects even better to center in the NFL. His initial quickness, balance and hand placement are exceptional. He is among the better zone-blocking interior linemen to come down the pike in years. 16. Dante Moore, QBOregon Ducks NFL Player Comp: C.J. Stroud, Texans Moore is the most precise passer of this class and that fact may earn him a top-10 selection in the 2027 draft, even if he hasn’t always played his best in big games. But Moore will first need to prove that he is healthy. Oregon coach Dan Lanning recently announced Moore is unlikely to return to the field this season after suffering a concussion following a late hit against USC in late September. The redshirt junior has another year of college eligibility remaining, should he want to use it. 15. Trevor Lauck, OTIowa Hawkeyes NFL Player Comp: Chris Lindstrom, Falcons Lauck is the latest star left tackle at Iowa, but his short arms may push him inside to guard in the NFL. Regardless of where he ultimately lines up at the pro level, his initial quickness, balance and core strength suggest a long and distinguished career. 14. Nick Marsh, WRIndiana Hoosiers NFL Player Comp: Christian Watson, Packers Hoosiers teammate Charlie Becker, understandably gets much of the hype, but Marsh is a first-round caliber receiver in his own right, boasting an even more exciting combination of size and athleticism. I expect the Michigan State transfer to rise throughout the draft process, as he’ll put up eye-popping numbers at the Scouting Combine. 13. Greg Johnson, OGMinnesota Golden Gophers NFL Player Comp: Frank Ragnow (retired) At 6-foot-6, 325 pounds, Johnson offers rare size for a guard and would be among the larger centers in NFL history. He’s starred at both positions over four seasons with the Gophers and will give his future NFL team a lot of flexibility on the inside. 12. Ellis Robinson IV, DBGeorgia Bulldogs NFL Player Comp: Denzel Ward, Browns Some cornerbacks just move differently. Robinson is so smooth it almost seems as if his backpedal, transition and acceleration should be naturally paired with music. Cornerbacks with his man-to-man cover skills don’t last long on draft day. 11. Arch Manning, QBTexas Longhorns NFL Player Comp: Justin Herbert, Chargers No quarterback in this class offers a better blend of traits than Manning, but this position requires more than just physical tools. While Manning’s frequent turnovers in high-pressure situations is an undeniable red flag, it's one that I believe can be cured with time and patience. 10. Ashton Hampton, DBClemson Tigers NFL Player Comp: Patrick Surtain Jr., Broncos Statistics don’t always tell the story with a prospect, but consider this one: Hampton has forced nearly as many incompletions (30) as he’s given up first downs (36) in his two and a half seasons of action at Clemson. Boasting prototypical size at 6-foot-2, 205 pounds, Hampton plays a highly aggressive and physical brand of ball that could have him pushing for top-10 consideration. 9. Drew Mestemaker, QBOklahoma State Cowboys NFL Player Comp: Josh Allen, Bills It is easy to get excited by Mestemaker’s dizzying ascent from high school backup to premium NFL prospect. His prototypical size, mobility and live arm will draw plenty of comparisons to Josh Allen in the pre-draft process. It is easy to forget now how raw Allen was coming out of Wyoming, however, and there are similar concerns about how quickly Mestemaker will adjust from the Air-Raid scheme he’s played in with the Cowboys and previously at North Texas. 8. Elijah Paige, OTUSC Trojans NFL Player Comp: Ronnie Stanley, Ravens The top-rated offensive tackle on my board, Paige has dominated blanked pass-rushers over his career, allowing just two total sacks in 27 career starts (all at left tackle). He’s not only quick and agile in pass protection, the 6-foot-7, 315-pounder also shows aggression and leg drive as a run blocker. 7. Trinidad Chambliss, QBOle Miss Rebels NFL Player Comp: Russell Wilson (retired) Between his compact frame, mobility, arm and poise, Chambliss possesses everything needed to project as a future franchise quarterback — except height. But NFL teams won’t repeat the mistake they made with Wilson by letting Chambliss slip to the third round. 6. Charlie Becker, WRIndiana Hoosiers NFL Player Comp: Larry Fitzgerald (retired) I’ll admit, I’m late to the party on Becker, previously typecasting him as "just" a big-red zone target. Upon closer inspection, however, Becker plays with grace and body control uncommon for a receiver with his 6-foot-4, 208-pound frame. He almost hovers with the ball in flight and uses his long arms and strong hands to create quite the catch radius. 5. Chris Cole, LBGeorgia Bulldogs NFL Player Comp: Fred Warner, 49ers Remember the rise Arvell Reese enjoyed a year ago as a part-time starter at Ohio State before becoming the No. 5 overall selection by the New York Giants? Cole is on a similar trajectory for Georgia. There is still some polishing that needs to happen, but he’s a remarkable athlete at 6-foot-3, 235 pounds, with a chance to ultimately become the best defender in this class. 4. Dylan Stewart, DESouth Carolina Gamecocks NFL Player Comp: Brian Burns, Giants Stewart promises to be one of the most heavily scrutinized players this year because while his tape is fantastic, the production is lacking. Stewart has 13 sacks in 28 career games with a notable drop in production over each of his three seasons. The traits are worth gambling on, however. Stewart has twitch, bend and underrated strength. If he commits to his craft, he should become an annual 10-plus sack a year player in the NFL. 3. Leonard Moore, DBNotre Dame Fighting Irish NFL Player Comp: Christian Gonzalez, Patriots After recording five interceptions during an All-American campaign a year ago, opponents have wisely ignored Moore’s side of the field this season. Moore pairs rare agility and smooth acceleration with prototypical size (6-foot-1, 197 pounds), as well as instincts and physicality. A likely top-10 selection, Moore is among the cleaner cornerback prospects in years. 2. Colin Simmons, DETexas Longhorns NFL Player Comp: Micah Parsons, Packers A recent high ankle sprain might keep Simmons sidelined for weeks, but that won’t stop a lucky NFL team from making him the first defensive player drafted this spring. In two and a half seasons, Simmons has proven himself to be nearly unblockable, recording a staggering 45.5 tackles for loss, 31.5 sacks and eight forced fumbles. The current injury and a troubling track record of penalties push Simmons to No. 2 on my board, but the gap between him and No. 1 is razor thin, with the Longhorns defender understandably ranking as the top overall prospect for some. 1. Jeremiah Smith, WROhio State Buckeyes NFL Player Comp: Julio Jones (retired) Far and away the best offensive player in this class, Smith offers a combination of size, speed and strength that only comes around every decade or so. I see a lot of similarities to Julio Jones — except Smith is even further along in his route-running at this point in his career.

articles.title: "Long standing beef": Patrick Mahomes sends clear message after Chiefs bring in Justin Tucker
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is keeping his focus on football as the Kansas City Chiefs welcome a familiar rival into their building.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is keeping his focus on football as the Kansas City Chiefs welcome a familiar rival into their building. Justin Tucker's arrival has raised eyebrows, not only because of Harrison Butker's recent struggles but also because of his past confrontation with Mahomes and Travis Kelce. However, the Chiefs quarterback has made one thing clear: there is no lingering tension between them. With Kansas City preparing for a crucial AFC West clash against Denver, Tucker's signing could have a much bigger impact than expected.Patrick Mahomes addresses past tension with Justin TuckerTucker's arrival in Kansas City brings back memories of an awkward moment before the 2023 AFC Championship Game. The Baltimore Ravens kicker had placed his equipment in an area where Mahomes and other Chiefs players were warming up.The situation quickly turned into a heated exchange. Kelce threw away Tucker's kicking tee and footballs, while Mahomes also became involved. The incident attracted plenty of attention, with questions about whether the players had developed a personal rivalry.However, Mahomes has dismissed suggestions of any lasting disagreement. Speaking to reporters on October 28, he explained that the incident was simply part of the competitive atmosphere surrounding such an important game.“I mean, the relationships, we haven’t had a lot of conversations ’cause he was obviously on the Ravens and I was on the Chiefs. But it wasn’t like we ever had any long standing beef or anything like that,” Mahomes said. “I think at that moment, it was just competitors being competitors. And it was a big moment for everybody’s career, and you’re playing the AFC Championship Game.“And he’s been a big-time kicker for a long time. And me and Trav were obviously competing and we wanted to go out there and win. And that stuff happened, but then you move on from that. I mean, at the end of the day, we’re just playing a game.”His comments suggest that the old disagreement will not affect Tucker's attempt to settle into his new team.Justin Tucker signing puts Harrison Butker under pressureThe Chiefs signed Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday after holding tryouts with three kickers. He impressed the coaching staff by converting all 30 attempts during the session, beating Harrison Mevis and Ben Sauls for the opportunity.Kansas City has a clear reason to explore another option. Butker has converted just 11 of 16 field-goal attempts through six games this season. His two misses against the Seattle Seahawks on October 25 proved particularly costly in the Chiefs' 20-3 defeat.Head coach Andy Reid has acknowledged the problem and expects Butker to respond.“He understands the business and how it works. We had a practice squad position open. For security, we brought (Tucker) in and put him in that spot that we had open. Butker gets it. He knows that’s part of the business. He’s struggled a little bit. He gets it, he needs to pick it up a little bit.”Tucker brings an impressive career record, including seven Pro Bowl selections and the second-highest field-goal percentage in NFL history. He also has experience performing under pressure, including his famous 47-yard overtime winner against Denver in the 2012 playoffs.For now, Butker remains Kansas City's kicker heading into Week 8. However, Tucker's arrival has created genuine competition. If Butker cannot rediscover his accuracy, the Chiefs may have little reason to keep waiting.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Packers' Josh Jacobs insists he wasn't making light of his arrest during TD celebration
articles.summary: Jacobs scored twice in his second game since returning to the Packers, but had a controversial celebration after one of them.
articles.body:
In just his second game back on the field with the Packers since being on the NFL's commissioner exempt list, Josh Jacobs helped power his team to a 27-19 win on Thursday night.

Jacobs finished with just 39 rushing yards, but added six catches and a pair of touchdowns in Green Bay's victory over Carolina. The running back's celebration after one of those scores, however, became controversial.

Jacobs, who was arrested earlier this year and charged with misdemeanor battery and destruction of property, appeared to put his hands behind his back as a touchdown celebration, but provided another explanation for his actions postgame.

Here's what Jacobs said about his touchdown celebration against the Panthers .

Josh Jacobs explains TD celebration vs. Panthers

After Jacobs scored his first touchdown of the night in the second quarter, he put his hands behind his back, leading fans to question whether he was making light of his arrest earlier in 2026.

In May, Jacobs was arrested in Wisconsin following an incident with a woman at his home. He was booked on five domestic battery-related charges, later charged with misdemeanor battery and destruction of property.

That incident led to Jacobs being placed on the commissioner's exempt list to start the 2026 season, missing six games before he was allowed to re-join the Packers las week. He remains subject to a potential NFL suspension for the league's personal conduct policy.

Fans criticized Jacobs for appearing to make light of his arrest, but the running back provided another explanation for his celebration against the Panthers, saying it was an ode to a gospel song called "Break Every Chain." He said that the broadcast didn't capture the full celebration.

"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said."It was f---ing one second that they just showed me."

Jacobs also said that he and teammate Savion Williams came up with two celebrations for his return.

"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was going to thank God -- that's what I did last week," Jacobs said. "The second one was going to be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was going to be the next celebration. It's just a correlation, but like I said, the media [is] going to run with it. They're going to make it something that it wasn't, but it is what it is."

The running back added that other Packers teammates did the same celebration.

"I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way," Jacobs said, per ESPN . "But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

articles.title: Dallas Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb said something wild about the Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb has never beaten the Cardinals since he was drafted by the Cowboys.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will face the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday in Week 8. The Cardinals are struggling this season, sitting at 2-5. But the Cowboys are 3-4 and have not beaten the Cardinals since 2017.

It has gotten the attention of receiver CeeDee Lamb, one of the best pass-catchers in the NFL.

Since he entered the league in 2020, he and the Cowboys have lost four times to the Cardinals, which led Lamb to say this about the matchup.

"Yeah, it's just crazy," Lamb said via Dallas' team site . "[We were] being very, very relaxed, and they punched us in the mouth every single time. They've always had more energy. They were more excited, regardless of if it was a 12 o'clock, Sunday night or Monday night.

"We've played them in prime time. They beat us there, so we need to treat them as if they are a Super Bowl-contending team, which they may be, you know what I'm saying? Hats off to them in their prep, and we've just got to go match them, if not overpower that."

The Cardinals certainly are not a Super Bowl-contending team. They have looked mostly like one of the worst teams in the NFL this season. However, they seem to find ways to win against the Cowboys.

The Cardinals have never lost at AT&T Stadium, which opened in 2009.

The Cowboys are seven-point home favorites in this game. The Cowboys and Cardinals kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday (11 a.m. Arizona time).

articles.title: Josh Allen vs Lamar Jackson: Two MVP careers, different playoff stories and one question about who will define the AFC era
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson meet Sunday at Highmark Stadium, and Jackson's ankle decides how much the game means.
articles.body: Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson meet Sunday at Highmark Stadium, and Jackson's ankle decides how much the game means. The Ravens quarterback has not played since Week 4 and missed three straight games. Coach Jesse Minter has sounded encouraging, though his status stayed unsettled this week. Buffalo is 5-1, Baltimore 4-3. Jackson has two MVP awards, Allen one, and neither has won a Super Bowl. Allen holds the playoff edge between them, winning both postseason meetings, in January 2021 and January 2025, but his exit in Denver last season showed that edge guarantees nothing in the AFC race.Josh Allen vs Lamar Jackson: Two MVP careers, two different playoff storiesJackson won MVP unanimously in 2019 and again in 2023. Allen took the award in 2024, and the vote was one of the closest in recent years. The stats show why. Jackson threw for 4,172 yards and 41 touchdowns with four interceptions that season, and ran for 915 yards. Allen threw for 3,731 yards and 28 touchdowns, but he also ran for 531 yards and 12 scores, and Buffalo finished 13-4 to Baltimore's 12-5.The playoffs split them. Jackson is 3-5 in the postseason. Their first meeting, a 17-3 Bills win, ended early for him because of a concussion. The second came in Buffalo in January 2025, when he threw an interception and lost a fumble in the first half. Allen scored twice on the ground, the Bills forced three turnovers, and Mark Andrews dropped a two-point try with 1:33 left in a 27-25 Buffalo win. Baltimore missed the playoffs the following season, so that night still closes out his résumé.Allen's story is messier, and last season made it worse. The AFC field had no Patrick Mahomes, Jackson or Joe Burrow, and Allen's team could not take advantage of that. Buffalo beat Jacksonville in the wild-card round, then lost 33-30 in overtime at Denver. Allen turned the ball over four times, after going 427 postseason snaps without a fumble or interception. "Feel like I let my teammates down tonight," he said afterward. He is also 0-7 in overtime games for his career.The two problems look different. Jackson's is a pattern across eight games. Allen's is a short list of bad endings, set against efficiency numbers that once ranked first among playoff quarterbacks since 2020. Allen has reached two AFC title games and Jackson one. Both lost to Kansas City.Sunday gives the AFC race an early testAcross seven meetings, Jackson has won three of five regular-season games, and Allen has won both playoff games. Oddsmakers still have the Bills favored on Sunday, even with Jackson possibly back. Baltimore lost its second straight game without him last weekend, and the Ravens average 395 yards in his starts this season.Minter is the Ravens' new head coach, and receiver Zay Flowers said in May that people would see a refreshed Jackson. The ankle has interrupted that plan. Jackson's 2025 was already injury-affected, so his health is a theme as much as his playoff record.Allen opened the year with 269 passing yards, 65 rushing yards and four total touchdowns in Week 1, and he leads the early MVP odds. He finished third in the vote last season, with two first-place votes. Matthew Stafford won it by one first-place vote over Drake Maye. Allen is also the first player in NFL history with five straight 40-touchdown seasons, counting passing and rushing.Sunday is not January. Still, Allen has beaten Jackson both times it counted most.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Dolphins weather forecast for NFL Week 8
articles.summary: Up-to-date weather forecast for Sunday’s game between the Patriots and Dolphins.
articles.body:
The last time the New England Patriots traveled to Florida, they were soundly beaten 35-6 by the Jacksonville Jaguars. One of the contributing factors to that loss appeared to be the team struggling with the heat and humidity.

At least one of the two might not have that big an impact come Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins. According to NFL Weather , temperatures at Hard Rock Stadium will not exceed 78°F during the Week 8 contest between the two division rivals. The National Weather Service , meanwhile, projects highs near 82°F for the day.

What will differentiate that game from the Jaguars one, however, is the precipitation. Whereas that Week 3 contest was played in sunny conditions, this one won't: the chance of rain has been calculated at 80% with showers and thunderstorms an option.

In addition, wind gusts of up to 26 mph are projected for the area (although in-stadium conditions may vary).

All in all, however, the weather could have an impact on the contest — as could the Patriots' conditioning.

"We have to be conditioned," said head coach Mike Vrabel this week. "The better that we play, the more we possess the ball, the fresher we'll stay defensively. Hopefully we get the receivers into a rotation. The backs, we rotate. I don't think that the offensive linemen will necessarily rotate. We may play a couple guys based on who's available. That remains to be seen. The edge guys, we rotate. We try to rotate along the defensive line. We like to have our best players available to help us win."

Kickoff between the Patriots and Dolphins on Sunday is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Jets, Titans, Browns will control the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft
articles.summary: The Jets, Browns, and Titans have made significant trades to boost their draft assets. We show how they control the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season has yet to hit the midway point.

But some teams — and their fans — are already thinking about the 2027 NFL Draft.

There is a long way to go until the league descends upon the nation's capital for the annual player entry draft, and many — many — mock drafts to come until then. And while the final order for the 2027 NFL Draft is far from finalized, some teams are already sitting in a very good position due to previous trades.

In fact three teams (the New York Jets, the Cleveland Browns, and the Tennessee Titans) already have multiple picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.

Will more teams join them as we approach the annual trade deadline?

Here is how the first round currently stands, as well as a look at the teams with multiple first-round picks, and how they got there.

Here is how the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft currently stands, bearing in mind there is a long way to go until this order is finalized:

Again, this is before all the games in Week 7 are played, so there is a long way to go until this order is finalized.

But if the draft were held today, the Chargers would have the first pick.

And the Jets would have three in the top 12.

Why the Jets, Browns, and Titans could control the 2027 NFL Draft

Ahead of the NFL's 2026 trade deadline three teams — the Jets, Browns, and Titans — have multiple first-round picks.

At the moment the Browns have a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. One is their own, which with Cleveland entering Week 7 with a 5-2 record, slots in at No. 26 for the moment.

The other comes from the Los Angeles Rams, courtesy of this summer's Myles Garrett trade. In that deal the Browns traded Garrett to the Rams in exchange for Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 conditional round pick (either a third-round pick, or a first-round pick if the Rams were to trade Garrett to a team in the AFC North).

With the Rams entering Week 7 with a 3-4 record, that pick slots in at No. 14 for the moment.

Like the Browns, the Titans currently hold a pair of picks in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. one is their own, which would be No. 2 as the Titans etner Week 7 with a 1-6 record.

The other? That comes from the Chicago Bears, thanks to Thursday's trade involving defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons. In that deal the Bears acquired Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2027 fourth-round pick, and a 2028 first-round pick.

With Chicago currently 5-2, the Bears' pick is at No. 28 at the moment.

Then we get to the Jets, who currently hold three first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft.

One is their own, which slots in at No. 11 for the moment thanks to New York's 2-5 record.

But their first, at least right now, would be at No. 7, thanks to the Indianapolis Colts. Last season the Jets traded cornerback Sauce Gardner to Indianapolis for wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, a 2026 first-round pick (which the Jets used at No. 16 to draft tight end Kenyon Sadiq), and a 2027 first-round pick.

Then their third pick comes, at least for the moment, from the Dallas Cowboys.

The Jets also traded defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to Dallas in exchange for defensive lineman Mazi Smith, a 2026 second-round pick (which the Jets then traded to the Detroit Lions in exchange for picks at No. 50 and No. 128 last year), and a 2027 first-round pick.

But that trade happened in November, after the preseason trade involving Micah Parsons. In August of 2025, the Cowboys sent Parsons to the Packers in exchange for Kenny Clark, a 2026 first-round pick (which Dallas traded to the Philadelphia Eagles), and a 2027 first-round pick.

Returning to the trade between the Jets and the Cowboys, the Jets will receive either the Cowboys' own first-round pick, or the pick Dallas received from Green Bay, whichever one is better.

At the moment, the Cowboys are 3-4, and after Thursday night's win over the Carolina Panthers, the Packers are 5-3. So if the 2027 NFL Draft were to happen today, the Jets' third pick would be the Cowboys' own selection at No. 12, and Dallas would be on the clock with Green Bay's pick at No. 20.

articles.title: Packers' Xavier McKinney says NFL fined him 'a lot' for  criticizing refs after loss to Lions
articles.summary: McKinney said the fine was at least $25,000, the minimum amount for criticizing officials.
articles.body:
Xavier McKinney said he was fined "a lot" of money by the NFL for ripping officials during his postgame comments following last Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions .

The Green Bay Packers safety, speaking after Thursday's 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers , would not divulge the exact amount, but the minimum fine for criticizing officiating is $25,000, as Puka Nacua found out last season . McKinney told reporters the total was at least that amount.

During the Lions game, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur got into numerous animated discussions with officials and said afterward there were "some tough calls." Those calls were a pair of roughing the passer penalties and an unnecessary roughness call.

LaFleur wasn't willing to pin the game on what he believed were bad calls. McKinney, on the other hand, didn't hold back, saying calls are "kind of f***ing up" games.

Understanding that his comments might draw a punishment from the NFL, McKinney didn't shy away from his criticism.

"I don't know how the NFL's going to treat it, but I'm not a big fan of the refs right now," McKinney said on Sunday. "I don't think it's great officiating, if I'm being completely honest. I think it's bulls*** a lot of the times." … "It's annoying even talking about it because these are critical drives throughout the game, and we might have a drive where we're getting stops but you're calling penalties and it's like, this is not a penalty," McKinney said. "To me, it just don't really make any sense, and it's killing our momentum, it's killing our drives, and it's kind of f***ing up the games, if I'm being honest."

"I don't know how the NFL's going to treat it, but I'm not a big fan of the refs right now," McKinney said on Sunday. "I don't think it's great officiating, if I'm being completely honest. I think it's bulls*** a lot of the times."

"It's annoying even talking about it because these are critical drives throughout the game, and we might have a drive where we're getting stops but you're calling penalties and it's like, this is not a penalty," McKinney said. "To me, it just don't really make any sense, and it's killing our momentum, it's killing our drives, and it's kind of f***ing up the games, if I'm being honest."

McKinney said he was fine with the league taking money out of his pocket because he felt his comments could help his team in the future.

The NFL reacted in another way to the officiating in that Packers-Lions game. According to Football Zebras , the officiating crew, led by Alex Moore, has been moved off of Sunday night's Philadelphia Eagles-Washington Commanders game and will now work the New England Patriots-Miami Dolphins matchup.

The switch is reportedly about "optics" and not any sort of disciplinary measure for the Packers-Lions crew.

articles.title: Week 8 Waiver Wire Pickups and Available Sleepers in Most Yahoo and Sleeper Leagues
articles.summary: Week 8 got underway with Thursday night's NFC showdown between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers. Another 13 games are on the schedule, and many fantasy managers will be looking for fill-ins to navigate it.
articles.body:
Week 8 got underway with Thursday night's NFC showdown between the Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers. Another 13 games are on the schedule, and many fantasy managers will be looking for fill-ins to navigate it.

In addition to numerous injuries, managers will have to deal with the Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers all being on bye.

While waiver claims have been processed in most leagues, a few viable spot starters may still be available in most Yahoo and Sleeper leagues. We'll dive into the top options for point-per-reception (PPR) play here.

The Atlanta Falcons will visit the rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers this week. To be fair, the Bucs haven't been overly friendly to opposing quarterbacks, allowing the sixth-fewest fantasy points to the position.

However, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. should still be viewed as a viable streamer this week. He topped 20 fantasy points in each of his past two games, and it's not as if Tampa has completely shut down opposing QBs weekly.

Two weeks ago, Aaron Rodgers engineered a comeback win over the Buccaneers and delivered a solid 17 fantasy points in the process. If Atlanta is unable to rely exclusively on Bijan Robinson and its running game, Penix should have a solid floor.

Penix is still only rostered in 22 percent of fantasy leagues.

Things may not go well for the Cleveland Browns and their running game when they face the Pittsburgh Steelers this week. Cleveland hasn't won a regular-season game in Pittsburgh since 2003, and the Steelers have surrendered the 10th-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Yet, Browns backup Dylan Sampson is worth flex consideration in Week 8 because of his role as a pass-catching back. He made his 2026 debut last week and finished with 10.7 fantasy points. He could have an even bigger outing this week if the Browns struggle to run the ball and/or spend the game playing from behind.

As a rookie last season, Sampson caught 33 passes and recorded 446 scrimmage yards.

Sampson is only really worth consideration in PPR leagues, but he's worth scooping up and keeping around for the foreseeable future. He's only rostered in 15 percent of leagues.

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

The Washington Commanders will be without No. 1 receiver Terry McLaurin for the remainder of the season. This should boost the fantasy value of Stefon Diggs and rookie wideout Antonio Williams.

Diggs has already been heavily rostered in fantasy leagues. Williams should have been a popular pickup this week after head coach Dan Quinn told reporters that he expects the rookie to help fill the void left by McLaurin.

Yet, Williams is still only rostered in 15 percent of fantasy leagues.

Williams hasn't produced double-digit fantasy points since Week 1, but he had eight points in Washington's last game and could easily be back to double digits this week. The Commanders will host the Philadelphia Eagles, who have surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing WRs.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, TE, Washington Commanders

With McLaurin out, the Commanders are also likely to heavily rely on tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo. The former Tennessee Titans standout hasn't always been a big part of Washington's game plan, but he has reached double-digit fantasy points in each of his past two games.

Okonkwo has also caught all 13 of his targets over his past two appearances. He should be heavily targeted against the Eagles, giving him a very solid PPR floor.

The Eagles' defense hasn't been as ineffective against opposing tight ends and has surrendered the seventh-fewest fantasy points to the position. However, volume could carry Okonkwo, who is only rostered in 25 percent of fantasy leagues.

*Fantasy roster and scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.body: Back in the 2026 offseason, NBC Sports studio analyst Matt Maiocco reported the San Francisco 49ers were offering Jauan Jennings a multi-year contract extension worth about $17 million per season. Jennings serves as a complementary, lower-volume target behind Jefferson, Addison, and tight end T.J. Hockenson.O’Connell reportedly uses Jennings for his physical size and run-blocking ability rather than as a primary option.The 6-foot-3, 212-pounder’s limited involvement is more than just visible and has raised questions about his future with the Vikings. This could give them additional flexibility to address other roster needs, as many believe at running back.NFL insider Adam Schefter reveals trade interestAs per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, even if Jauan Jennings has emerged as a potential trade target, Minnesota is not actively shopping him.
