articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Khalil Mack, Quentin Johnston, 'Inquiries' for Chargers' Vet Players
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers reportedly aren't yet willing to sell off veteran players despite getting off to an 0-6 start this season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers reportedly aren't yet willing to sell off veteran players despite getting off to an 0-6 start this season.

According to SI.com's Albert Breer , the Chargers have "shut down trade inquiries" thus far, as general manager Joe Hortiz and head coach Jim Harbaugh aren't yet looking to "wave any sort of white flag."

Pass-rusher Khalil Mack and wide receiver Quentin Johnston are two players Breer mentioned as having "questions" around them regarding their availability, but the Chargers reportedly aren't ready to start a fire sale yet.

L.A. is the last winless team remaining in the NFL this season, and unless the Chargers essentially run the table, it seems unlikely that the playoffs are in their immediate future.

The Bolts' schedule only appears to be getting tougher as well with a game against the Los Angeles Rams this weekend, followed by the Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens the two weeks after that.

When the Chargers host the Texans on Nov. 8, the game will be played two days before the NFL trade deadline, and if Los Angeles loses one or even both of its next two games, perhaps the organization's stance will change.

It would be especially logical for the Chargers to move on from players set to hit free agency during the offseason, especially if they don't have designs on signing them to a new deal.

Mack, 35, signed a one-year deal to return to the Chargers this past offseason, and since he is nearing the end of his illustrious career, one would think he would like the chance to contend for a Super Bowl this season and perhaps even next season.

With three sacks through six games this season, Mack could provide a boost to a contender, and the Chargers would not only be doing him a favor by trading him, but they would be getting an asset back for a player they could lose for nothing in a few months anyway.

Trading a player like Johnston is less cut and dry since he is significantly younger than Mack and is signed through next season.

Originally selected 21st overall in the 2023 NFL draft by the Chargers, the 25-year-old Johnston has failed to live up to expectations.

He showed flashes last season and set a career high with 735 receiving yards, while also matching a career high with eight touchdowns, but he hasn't come close to that level this season.

Through five games, Johnston has registered just eight catches for 165 yards and no touchdowns.

Perhaps the Chargers would be willing to move Johnston if a team wants to take on his $16.4 million salary cap hit for next season, but it is fair to wonder if any team would want to do that given Johnston's lack of production this season.

articles.title: Greg Olsen Reportedly Seen as 'Favorite' to Replace Troy Aikman on 'Monday Night Football'
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing speculation about Troy Aikman's future in the Monday Night Football broadcast booth, ESPN is keeping an eye on Greg Olsen as a potential replacement candidate.
articles.body:
Amid the ongoing speculation about Troy Aikman's future in the Monday Night Football broadcast booth, ESPN is keeping an eye on Greg Olsen as a potential replacement candidate.

Per The Athletic's Andrew Marchand , Olsen is viewed as the "favorite" by people in the sports media industry to take over Aikman's role next to Joe Buck next season.

Sports media insider Richard Deitsch reported on Oct. 15 that Olsen's current contract with Fox is set to expire at the end of this season and the two sides have not had any discussions about a new deal thus far.

Aikman and Buck have been broadcast partners since 2002. They spent 20 seasons together at Fox before signing with ESPN in March 2022 to take over as the commentary crew for Monday Night Football.

This season marks the final year of the original contracts Aikman and Buck signed with ESPN. Buck got a new six-year deal from the network in September, leaving Aikman's status up in the air right now.

During an Oct. 16 appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas, Aikman said he is going to "free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens."

Olsen has been a full-time broadcaster as part of Fox Sports' NFL coverage since the 2021 season. He was part of the No. 1 team with play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt and sideline reporters Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi during the 2022 season.

That group was on the call for Super Bowl 57 between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles.

After Tom Brady moved into broadcasting starting in 2023, Olsen has been paired with Joe Davis on the No. 2 team for Fox.

articles.title: Panthers Fire DC Ejiro Evero, Todd Wash Named Interim After Losses to Packers, Bucs
articles.summary: After allowing 70 points in two losses over the past four days, the Carolina Panthers are making a change at defensive coordinator.
articles.body:
After allowing 70 points in two losses over the past four days, the Carolina Panthers are making a change at defensive coordinator.

Panthers head coach Dave Canales announced on Friday that Ejiro Evero has been fired and defensive line coach Todd Wash will take over as defensive coordinator for the remainder of the season.

The Panthers also fired defensive pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley.

Carolina followed up a 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday with a 27-19 defeat against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night.

The Panthers have allowed at least 26 points in four of their six games this season. Their season started by giving up 59 points and 552 yards to the Chicago Bears in Week 1. Both of those remain the highest single-game totals for any team in 2026.

Overall, the Panthers rank 27th in points allowed and 30th in rushing yards allowed per game. Their 12 rushing touchdowns allowed are the most by any defense.

Evero was in his fourth season as Carolina's defensive coordinator. He was hired in February 2023 by then-head coach Frank Reich and remained in his role after Canales took over in January 2024.

After finishing 29th and 32nd in points allowed during Evero's first two years as defensive coordinator, 2025 saw the unit take a step forward. The defense ranked 15th in points allowed, its highest ranking in that category since 2017.

Carolina was expected to take a step forward this season after making the playoffs last season. The offense has largely done its part with 25.4 points per game, ninth-best in the NFL.

But the struggles on defense are leading to the Panthers slowly falling down the NFC standings. Playing in the NFC South does help, as their 3-4 record has them tied with the Atlanta Falcons for first place.

Wash is also in his fourth season with the Panthers as a holdover from Reich's staff in 2023. He has five years of experience as a defensive coordinator from 2016 to '20 when he was with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Carolina has a few extra days of rest before returning to play in Week 9 against the Denver Broncos at Bank of America Stadium.

articles.title: Jeffery Simmons Thanks Titans Fans After Blockbuster Trade to Bears, 'The Emotions Have Been High'
articles.summary: Star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons thanked the Tennessee Titans organization and Titans fans on Friday following his trade to the Chicago Bears this week.
articles.body:
Star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons thanked the Tennessee Titans organization and Titans fans on Friday following his trade to the Chicago Bears this week.

In an Instagram post, Simmons wrote that "emotions have been high," adding that he "never thought" he would be writing a farewell message to the only home he has ever known at the NFL level:

The struggling Titans decided to part ways with Simmons on Thursday, sending him and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Bears in exchange for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, and a 2027 fourth-round pick.

Simmons' message, which saw him express his love and appreciation for the city of Nashville, came on the heels of the Titans paying tribute to him with an X post on Thursday night:

Originally selected 19th overall by the Titans in the 2019 NFL draft out of Mississippi State, Simmons established himself as one of the elite defensive tackles in the league during his eight-year tenure in Tennessee.

A four-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro, Simmons has recorded 46.5 sacks, 414 tackles and 72 tackles for loss in 106 career NFL regular-season games.

While Simmons never reached or won a Super Bowl with the Titans, he helped take them to the playoffs three times, including a trip to the AFC Championship Game in 2019.

Simmons has gotten better with age as well, setting new career highs in sacks (11), TFLs (17) and forced fumbles (three) last season.

He is also on a strong pace this season with 38 tackles and four sacks through seven games.

Despite Simmons' strong play, the Titans are just 1-6 this season, and they made the decision to part ways with their best player even though he is signed through 2030.

In Chicago, Simmons will have a chance to make the Bears legitimate Super Bowl contenders.

On the strength of head coach Ben Johnson's offense, the Bears fell just short of the NFC Championship Game last season, and after a 5-2 start, they look to be in the mix once again this season.

Simmons is the type of difference-maker Chicago's defense was missing, and with him now leading the defense and quarterback Caleb Williams leading the offense, the Bears will be a tough out come January.

articles.title: Travis Kelce vs Patrick Mahomes: Which Chiefs superstar has made a bigger impact through charitable donations and community work?
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have built extraordinary careers in Kansas City, winning championships and earning millions along the way.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have built extraordinary careers in Kansas City, winning championships and earning millions along the way. But their influence extends well beyond the football field. Both Chiefs superstars have invested heavily in charitable causes, supported children from disadvantaged backgrounds and helped strengthen their communities through their respective foundations. From Kelce's nearly $2 million contribution to Operation Breakthrough to Mahomes' multimillion-dollar grants for youth organisations, their generosity has become an important part of their legacies. While their approaches differ, their shared commitment raises an interesting question: Which Chiefs star has made a bigger impact through charity?Travis Kelce's charity work focuses on education and opportunities for underserved childrenKelce's charitable journey began with a personal connection to the struggles faced by young people. Growing up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, the tight end saw how access to resources and opportunities could shape a child's future. That experience inspired him to establish the Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation in 2015.The organisation aims to help disadvantaged young people develop skills through education, business, athletics, science, technology, engineering, mathematics and the arts. Rather than limiting its work to financial assistance, Kelce's foundation focuses on giving children the tools to build independent futures.One of his most significant commitments has been his partnership with Operation Breakthrough, a Kansas City nonprofit that supports children and families experiencing poverty. Kelce has contributed nearly $2 million to the organisation over the years through personal donations and directed funds, according to the Kansas City Chiefs.His most ambitious project with the organisation is the Ignition Lab. In 2020, Kelce announced plans to purchase an old building in Kansas City and transform it into a learning and workforce development centre for teenagers. The project became a reality in 2021, providing students aged 14 to 18 with opportunities to explore careers in engineering, automotive work, coding, digital media and entrepreneurship.The centre has helped more than 1,000 students since opening. Its purpose goes beyond classroom lessons, allowing teenagers to gain practical experience and discover possible career paths before entering adulthood.Kelce has also supported his hometown through the Heights Schools Foundation. His contributions have helped more than 2,300 children access remote learning, after-school programmes, tutoring and inspirational speakers.His generosity became particularly visible following the February 2024 Kansas City parade shooting. Two young sisters from the Reyes family suffered gunshot wounds during the incident. Kelce's Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation made two separate $50,000 donations to their family's fundraiser, bringing the total contribution to $100,000. The money helped cover their medical recovery and future needs.He has continued supporting Operation Breakthrough through annual fundraising events. His Celebrity Challenge brings together athletes from Kansas City's professional sports teams to raise money for the nonprofit. In October 2026, the event returned for its seventh edition.Kelce has also won Nationwide's Charity Challenge three times. His latest victory in January 2026 secured another $35,000 donation for Operation Breakthrough. He previously earned the same award in 2020 and 2025, making him the first three-time winner of the programme.Patrick Mahomes' foundation has distributed millions to children's charitiesWhile Kelce has built a strong connection with a few major organisations, Mahomes has developed a wider charitable network through his 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.Established in 2019, the foundation focuses on improving children's lives through health, education, wellness and community support. Patrick and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have backed several projects across Kansas City and Texas, with grants reaching schools, youth organisations and community programmes.One of their biggest contributions came in 2021, when the foundation donated $1 million towards the redevelopment of Martin Luther King Jr. Park in Kansas City. The funding helped create an inclusive playground where children with different physical and mental abilities could play together.The project became an important community space, with accessible equipment and features designed to welcome children of all abilities. Mahomes also attended the opening ceremony, celebrating the playground with local families.In October 2023, the foundation announced another major commitment. It pledged $1.625 million to Boys & Girls Clubs of America through a multi-year partnership. The contribution supports children in Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, Texas.The partnership also introduced an additional fundraising element. The foundation committed to donating $1,500 for every regular-season touchdown scored by Mahomes, creating another way to connect his NFL performances with youth development.His foundation has also supported food security and children's healthcare. In 2022, it distributed more than 15,000 meals through food bank partnerships and worked with OneSight Vision Clinic to provide free eye examinations and glasses to more than 100 children in the Kansas City area.Mahomes has also supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, granting wishes to 10 children with serious illnesses. His involvement included spending time with young fans and helping create memorable experiences for their families.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce support different causes through their foundationsTheir charitable work shares a common goal, but the way they approach it reveals two different priorities.Kelce has built much of his philanthropic identity around long-term involvement. His relationship with Operation Breakthrough goes beyond writing cheques. He regularly visits the organisation, spends time with students and helps create programmes that can support children as they grow older.His foundation also supports educational opportunities in Cleveland Heights and Kansas City. The University of Cincinnati has benefited from his support through a health and wellness endowment for student-athletes.Mahomes, meanwhile, has developed a grant-based approach that reaches a wider network of organisations. His foundation has supported groups such as Lead to Read, City Year, United Way of Greater Kansas City, Children's Mercy Hospital, Special Olympics Missouri and Kansas City Public Library.The foundation's 2024 financial records provide an idea of its reach. According to nonprofit financial data, 15 and the Mahomies distributed approximately $4.6 million through 119 grants between 2020 and 2024. Its 2024 grants included $650,000 for Boys & Girls Clubs of America, $57,500 for City Year, $50,500 for Lead to Read and $50,000 for United Way of Greater Kansas City.Mahomes has also encouraged young people to become active in their communities through programmes such as Read for 15 and Volunteer for 15. These initiatives encourage children to spend time reading and helping others rather than focusing only on receiving financial assistance.The foundation has supported scholarship programmes, food assistance and inclusive sports opportunities as well. Its work with Special Olympics Missouri and other youth organisations reflects a broader effort to reach children with different needs.Who has made a bigger charitable impact, Travis Kelce or Patrick Mahomes?Comparing the two Chiefs stars through a single donation figure would miss much of the story. Their foundations operate differently, and their financial records cover different periods.Kelce has contributed nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough alone, while his work with Ignition Lab has created lasting educational and career opportunities for teenagers. His $100,000 contribution to the Reyes family and repeated fundraising victories also demonstrate his willingness to support families facing difficult circumstances.Mahomes has a wider documented grant portfolio. His foundation distributed approximately $4.6 million across 119 grants between 2020 and 2024, alongside major commitments such as the $1 million playground project and the $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs partnership.However, the foundation's grant totals should not be treated as Mahomes' personal donations. They include money raised and distributed through the charitable organisation and its partners. The same distinction applies to Kelce's foundation contributions.What stands out is how both players have turned their success into opportunities for others. Kelce has developed a close connection with young people through education and career development, while Mahomes has used his foundation to support a wider range of organisations.Their approaches may be different, but their impact reaches beyond football. For Kansas City, having two of its biggest sporting stars invest in the next generation could prove just as meaningful as the trophies they have won.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chiefs’ Justin Tucker decision triggers media clash as Emmanuel Acho turns Mina Kimes and Nick Wright’s criticism against them
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decision to sign Justin Tucker has sparked a debate that goes beyond the veteran kicker’s ability on the field.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decision to sign Justin Tucker has sparked a debate that goes beyond the veteran kicker’s ability on the field. ESPN analysts Mina Kimes and Nick Wright questioned the move, raising concerns about the risks of bringing Tucker into Kansas City. Emmanuel Acho, however, challenged their criticism, turning the discussion toward the standards used to judge the Chiefs’ decision. The disagreement highlights a difficult question for the team: how much risk should a contender accept when looking for answers at a position where one missed kick can change a game?Emmanuel Acho challenges Mina Kimes and Nick Wright over their Justin Tucker criticismAcho’s response focused less on Tucker’s kicking record and more on what he sees as inconsistent standards across the NFL. The former linebacker argued that critics cannot single out one player while continuing to support a league where other players have faced serious allegations or been involved in troubling incidents.“If you want to call out Justin Tucker, which I have no issue with you doing, you’ve got to call out everybody on every team, including coaches,” Acho said.His argument was direct. Acho acknowledged the seriousness of the allegations against Tucker but questioned why the backlash appeared focused on one case. He also challenged Kimes and Wright to consider their roles as analysts who continue to cover and celebrate the sport.The controversy is not based on a settled finding of wrongdoing. In 2025, The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists accused Tucker of sexual misconduct. The allegations concerned incidents at eight Baltimore-area spas and wellness centers between 2012 and 2016. Tucker has denied the accusations, calling them “unequivocally false.”Kimes drew attention to the allegations after the Chiefs announced the signing, sharing a screenshot of the report on social media. Wright was more explicit about his opposition, writing, “Going on the record that I hope Justin Tucker never plays a snap for the Chiefs.”Acho challenged both commentators over the difference between condemning a player and continuing to support the wider league. His criticism raises a genuine question about where sports media figures should draw the line, although opposing a signing does not automatically require someone to stop covering the NFL.Chiefs’ kicking problems add another layer to the debateKansas City’s decision also has a clear football explanation. Harrison Butker has struggled this season, missing five of his 16 field-goal attempts. His latest difficulties came in the Chiefs’ 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, when he missed two kicks and Kansas City managed only three points.Tucker, a five-time All-Pro, offers a chance to assess an experienced kicker who was once among the NFL’s most reliable. However, he has not played in an NFL game since 2024. He also missed the entire 2025 season after receiving a 10-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy.Chiefs coach Andy Reid offered little detail when asked about the decision, saying, “He’s done his suspension. Took care of his business there. I’ll leave it at that.”For now, Tucker is on the practice squad, while Butker remains Kansas City’s kicker on the active roster. The signing does not guarantee Tucker will play, and the Chiefs still have to decide whether his potential on the field outweighs the questions surrounding his return.That distinction matters. Kansas City can evaluate Tucker as a possible solution to its kicking problems, but the move also brings scrutiny that cannot be settled by statistics alone. Acho has shifted the debate toward the consistency of the media’s response, while Kimes and Wright have made their objections clear. The Chiefs must now deal with both the football decision and the public reaction it has created.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The Chicago Bears revealed that four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who officially arrived in town via trade on Thursday, will wear No. 99.

The Bears acquired Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick from the Titans for 2027 and 2028 first-round selections and a 2027 fourth-round choice.

Simmons wore No. 98 for seven-plus seasons with Tennessee. However, Bears defensive end Montez Sweat—who was college teammates with Simmons at Mississippi State—has No. 98.

The former Bulldogs star had his best NFL season in 2025, amassing a career-high 11 sacks, 67 tackles (39 solo) and 21 quarterback hits. He earned All-Pro First Team honors.

Simmons has continued his standout play in 2026, racking up four sacks, 38 tackles (20 solo) and nine quarterback hits in seven games.

Now the 5-2 Bears have him aboard just in time for a huge NFC battle on Monday evening at the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Colts' Josh Downs to Play vs. Jaguars Despite Reported Trade Request Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs will play Sunday at the Jacksonville Jaguars despite his trade request, head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Friday.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs will play Sunday at the Jacksonville Jaguars despite his trade request , head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Friday.

The 2-5 Colts have already traded left guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers amid a disappointing year that has included the firing of general manager Chris Ballard on Oct. 19.

Downs is in his fourth NFL season and the final year of his rookie contract. The former UNC star, who was a third-round pick in the 2023 draft, has caught 26 passes for 307 yards in seven games this year.

One can safely assume his time with the Colts is arriving at its end, whether it's via a trade before the Nov. 10 deadline or in free agency next offseason.

It's possible the end could happen sooner rather than later.

Teams are certainly in need of wide receiver help. Of note, NFL insider James Palmer reported on Prime on Thursday night that the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers are both looking for wideouts.

The Colts have already made it clear that they are conducting a fire sale as they presumably enter a rebuild, so trading Downs before he can leave for nothing in free agency makes sense.

In the meantime, Indianapolis is forging ahead amid a tough season that's seen the team lose three straight. A hard matchup at the 4-2 and first-place Jaguars now looms. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson's Status for Ravens vs. Bills Revealed by Jesse Minter amid Ankle Injury
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday he'll be back on the field Sunday against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday he'll be back on the field Sunday against the Buffalo Bills.

Jackson told reporters he's feeling "better" after being diagnosed with a high ankle sprain.

Jackson's exact status has been something of a question mark, as he practiced some before Baltimore's game against the Cincinnati Bengals but didn't take the field.

Minter was asked about the overall messaging surrounding the injury since he previously called Jackson "day-to-day" while the quarterback said it was a high ankle sprain that prevented him from running.

"When the player is healthy enough to play, they'll play," Minter said while also reiterating the team will know more Wednesday. "… There's things that change sometimes with injuries and what you think of it right when it happens in a game where the adrenaline and things are still going on."

Tyler Huntley has played for Jackson during the starter's absence and led the team to a victory over the Atlanta Falcons before losing to the Cleveland Browns and Bengals in AFC North games.

Baltimore is now 4-3 overall but 0-2 in the division and in last place.

The Ravens will look to get back in the win column Sunday when Jackson is back under center to face Josh Allen and the Bills.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs says hands-behind-back gesture after first-half TD vs. Panthers was ode to gospel song
articles.summary: Jacobs was arrested in May and ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs told reporters postgame Thursday night that his first-half touchdown celebration was an ode to the gospel song "Break Every Chain."

After scoring from 1 yard out in the second quarter of a 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field , the Prime Video broadcast showed a glimpse of the controversial celebration , which began with him putting his hands behind his back.

That clip instantly circulated online, with many interpreting that gesture as Jacobs mocking his May arrest, for which he ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property .

Jacobs was clearly bothered by that connection and denied it.

"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said, via ESPN's Rob Demovsky , noting, "It was f***ing one second that they just showed me."

Jacobs explained that he and Packers wide receiver Savion Williams came up with the celebration.

"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was going to thank God — that's what I did last week," Jacobs said. "The second one was going to be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was going to be the next celebration. It's just a correlation, but, like I said, the media [is] going to run with it. They're going to make it something that it wasn't, but it is what it is."

Not long after the 28-year-old Jacobs hopped into the end zone to give the Packers a 13-10 lead, he put his hands behind his back and walked forward a couple steps. Later, Jacobs and Williams can be seen completing the celebration together.

"I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way," Jacobs said, per ESPN . "But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

Jacobs finished the night with 39 rushing yards on 21 carries, averaging a mere 1.9 yards per tote. He did score that TD, though, along with another one in third quarter on a 4-yard reception. The three-time Pro Bowl back caught six passes for 13 yards in the victory.

He landed on that list in the aftermath of his spring altercation with a woman at his Green Bay area home .

Back in September, Jacobs was reportedly convicted of battery and fined $1,000. Additionally, per ESPN , he accepted a deferred judgment agreement on the criminal damage to property charge.

Jacobs was reportedly ordered to pay restitution, attend counseling, avoid contact with the victim and be supervised for one year.

Upon being removed from the commissioner exempt list earlier this month, Jacobs said he was "remorseful" and "sorry for putting this team in this situation."

At the time, he added, among other things: "Going forward just trying to be better. I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lotta people that know me in this locker room, or that's been around me, I'll let them do that."

The NFL's investigation into Jacobs' potential violations of the personal conduct policy is ongoing. Once that investigation wraps, Jacobs could receive a suspension from the league. That said, time served on the commissioner exempt list can count toward a suspension.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Mike Tomlin's Potential Return, 'High Demand' Ahead of Coaching Carousel
articles.summary: Football Night in America analyst and ex-Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin would reportedly be in "extremely high demand" if he left the broadcast booth back for the sidelines, but "it's not considered automatic" that he'd make the return, per Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.
articles.body:
Football Night in America analyst and ex-Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin would reportedly be in "extremely high demand" if he left the broadcast booth back for the sidelines, but "it's not considered automatic" that he'd make the return, per Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.

"Mike Tomlin is expected to be in extremely high demand as an NFL head coaching candidate in the coming months, but it's not considered automatic that he would leave his broadcasting job at NBC to accept a big-money coaching offer, sources tell Front Office Sports.

"It's believed that Tomlin's contract with NBC would allow him to depart the network for an NFL coaching job. But other factors, such as the demands of coaching as compared to those in his promising broadcasting career, are expected to receive consideration, according to those sources."

Report: Olsen 'Favorite' to Replace Aikman

Tomlin, 54, spent 19 seasons (2007-2025) as the Steelers' head coach, going 193-114-2, making 13 playoff appearances and winning eight AFC North titles, two AFC Championships and one Super Bowl.

After the 2025 season, Tomlin stepped down as head coach. He now has a great gig with NBC, which he seems to be enjoying quite well.

So no one can blame Tomlin if he decides the broadcasting life is for him in the present and future.

However, if Tomlin wants to get back into coaching, it's no surprise teams would be calling given his tremendous resume and lengthy history of success.

None of Tomlin's teams ever finished with a record under .500, and making the playoffs more often than not over two decades is a remarkable feat.

Head coaching positions always open up in the NFL. In fact, there have been at least five head coaching changes in each of the last 16 seasons, including 10 coaching changes last offseason, per ESPN .

Tomlin should therefore have his chance to head back to the NFL if he wants. The question is whether that'll be the case.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Reveals Stipulation Required to Make Trade at 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: In the aftermath of three NFC playoff contenders making significant trades to improve their rosters this week, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't necessarily feeling pressure to respond with a deal of his own.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of three NFC playoff contenders making significant trades to improve their rosters this week, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't necessarily feeling pressure to respond with a deal of his own.

Appearing on Friday's episode of The K&C Masterpiece on 105.3 The Fan (h/t The Athletic's Jon Machota ), Jones said the Cowboys would need to find a "dynamic situation to give up picks" in a trade.

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

The NFC landscape was altered dramatically this week. It started on Tuesday when the Seattle Seahawks added Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts, followed a few hours later by the San Francisco 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner.

Things hit another level on Thursday when the Chicago Bears traded two first-round picks to the Chicago Bears in a package All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

Dallas is in a bit of an awkward position with less than two weeks remaining before the trade deadline. The Cowboys sit at 3-4 through seven games, two games behind the New York Giants in the loss column for first place in the NFC East.

Their issues from last season have carried over into 2026, with the defense frequently holding back one of the league's best offenses. They rank 23rd in points allowed, 27th in defensive success rate and 30th in EPA allowed per play.

Another issue, along with their current spot in the standings, is how much the Cowboys have invested over the past 12 months in trying to figure out their defense.

Jones sent a 2028 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for Joey Porter Jr. on Oct. 1. Prior to last year's trade deadline, he gave up a 2027 first-round pick to the New York Jets for Quinnen Williams.

Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals has started to pop up as a potential trade target for the Cowboys, but it could depend on the cost if Dallas can make it happen.

The Cowboys currently only have four picks in the upcoming draft. Hypothetically, if they were to send a 2027 second-rounder to Arizona, all of their own picks would be gone. Their selections would be coming from the Green Bay Packers (first round), Pittsburgh Steelers (fourth round) and New England Patriots (seventh round).

articles.title: Appeals court reverses rejection of damages award against NFL in Sunday Ticket class action
articles.summary: NFL undoubtedly will appeal the ruling to the U.S. Supreme Court.
articles.body:
This is the kind of Friday afternoon bad news dump that counts as horrible news for the NFL.

Via Mike Scarcella of Reuters, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit has reinstated the $4.7 billion verdict in the Sunday Ticket class action.

The Reuters article, however, apparently has misread the decision. Mark Maske of Front Office Sports characterizes the outcome as ordering a new trial on damages .

"The jury clearly awarded damages based on its improper consideration of the evidence rather than according to the district court's instructions," the Ninth Circuit wrote. "This warrants a new trial on damages. We remand this case for the district court to reinstate the jury's liability verdict and hold a new damages trial."

A new trial on damages could result in a lower (or similar or, in theory, higher) final verdict.

The original award, given by a jury in July 2024, was scrapped by the presiding judge over concerns regarding the evidence the plaintiffs presented of economic harm. The judge did not throw out the finding that the NFL had violated federal antitrust laws in the pricing of the Sunday Ticket package.

If/when any verdict becomes an official judgment, the damages will be tripled.

The original verdict sent shock waves through the league, since it ultimately would require each team to come up with $440 million in cash. Statutory interest will push that number even higher.

The NFL undoubtedly will appeal the final decision to the U.S. Supreme Court, which would first have to decide whether to accept the case before issuing a decision. The case possibly would not be ripe for an appeal to the Supreme Court until a new trial on damages happens — if that's what the Ninth Circuit has indeed ordered.

Whatever happens next, the situation instantly becomes the most consequential piece of litigation in the 100-plus-year history of the league.

articles.title: 'Punt' on this year's quarterback draft class, take Jeremiah Smith, says college football expert Brooks Austin
articles.summary: Film expert Brooks Austin says no 2027 NFL Draft quarterback deserves a top pick and would take Jeremiah Smith as the No. 1 overall prospect.
articles.body: While the NFL Draft isn't until next April, that never stops general managers, scouts and even fans from opining on what their teams will do in the spring. It's the main reason why mock drafts exist and are created nearly a year in advance, because everyone is dying to know who their favorite team is going to select with their first round pick. Of course, because it's the most important position on the field, the quarterback draws the most amount of eyes when it comes to the first round of the draft, and the 2027 edition is no exception. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! There are several draft-eligible signal callers who are generating plenty of buzz, but one expert thinks this might be the year to skip out on the position altogether if a team holds a top pick. Brooks Austin has made a living studying college football film, so much so that he's earned the moniker "The Film Guy." His YouTube channel, "The Film Guy Network," has over 135,000 subscribers, and he's recently parlayed that into a partnership with the college football media giant On3. Suffice to say, Austin knows ball, so when I sat down with him to talk about the college game, and more specifically, the quarterback class for the 2027 NFL Draft, he gave a surprising assessment. "Can I punt on the entire class," he asked, half jokingly. As Austin points out, there are some solid quarterbacks in this class, but none are the "can't miss" prospects that would necessitate a top-five pick like in years past. Most experts figured Oregon's Dante Moore would be the first QB off the board in '27, given he was already projected to go high last year before deciding to return to Eugene. An injury might have derailed that for Moore, but as Austin points out, the injured Duck wasn't without some limitations of his own even before exiting for the season. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "Dante Moore is a really good football player," he explains. "But (he) gets stuck on reads and makes his mind up pre-snap, and that scares me. He's also a little up and down, like from a fundamental standpoint, from a mechanics standpoint, he just kinda gets away with a lot of it in college football." Moore wasn't the only one giving Austin some pause. Ole Miss's Trinidad Chambliss, one of the preseason Heisman favorites, has had a fine season statistically, but his build makes Austin nervous about him at the next level. "I love him, but there are some physical questions about that one as well, like, is he gonna work at his stature when we get to the league?" Other quarterbacks like Texas' Arch Manning and LSU's Sam Leavitt get mentioned as well, with Austin stating question marks about their decision making and turnover problems. The prospect who Austin believes should go number one overall shouldn't come as a shock to anyone who watches football on Saturday. "If I had the number one overall pick, I'd draft Jeremiah Smith," Austin admits. "And then next year I try to find a quarterback." Austin explains that Smith, the Ohio State wide receiver, is a "guarantee" and one of the only truly generational prospects we've seen in the game since Andrew Luck in 2012. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I would draft Smith, and I'd be like, 'I've got the best prospect and most known prospect that's come out of college football... since maybe like Andrew Luck,'" Austin claims. "I would just draft him if I was bad enough to be the number one overall pick."

articles.title: Cardinals' Budda Baker Wears Halloween Mask to Press Conference, Addresses NFL Trade Rumors in Video
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker was very much in the Halloween spirit during his media availability on Friday.
articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker was very much in the Halloween spirit during his media availability on Friday.

While discussing multiple subjects, including the Cardinals' road game against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Baker wore a scary clown mask:

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

Baker even talked about the possibility of getting dealt ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, saying, "I just live in the present, like today having a great time with you guys. Gonna have a great Friday practice and just focus on playing against the Dallas Cowboys, and trying to get a W at their stadium."

Given the fact that the Cards have only reached the playoffs once during Baker's 10-year run with the organization, he has often been the subject of trade rumors and speculation.

That continues to be the case this season, as ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported this week that Baker is expected to generate "strong interest" if made available. Fowler added that sources he has spoken to believe Arizona should "try to get something" for the 30-year-old veteran.

That doesn't guarantee that the Cardinals won't look to move Baker, though, especially since he is only signed through 2027.

At 2-5, Arizona is not looking like a playoff contender this season, and it may be a while before the team is back in the mix.

By the time that happens, Baker may be past his prime or already moved on to a different team via free agency.

Baker is an eight-time Pro Bowler and two-time First Team All-Pro with 1,065 tackles, 13.5 sacks and nine interceptions in 145 career games.

There is little doubt that contending teams would love to get their hands on Baker if possible, and if the Cards continue to lose, that could potentially become a reality by the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

articles.title: Falcons rookie Anterio Thompson says he was diagnosed with career-ending 'genetic mutation' in spinal cord: 'I was told I would never play football again'
articles.summary: Thompson was placed on Atlanta's non-football injury list in July.
articles.body:
It appears that Atlanta Falcons rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson will not be taking the field. Thompson, who was placed on the non-football injury list this summer, revealed on Thursday that he had been sidelined due to a career-ending "genetic mutation" on his spinal cord.

Thompson posted the news on his Instagram story on Thursday, which was his 24th birthday. The tackle wrote that he was told about the mutation on May 8 — just two weeks after the Falcons selected him in the sixth round.

"Blessed to make it to 24. Mentally, I've been better than anyone would be in my situation," Thompson wrote. "I was told I would never play football again due to a genetic mutation in my spinal cord that I had no idea about."

In the post, Thompson wrote that he believes "everything happens for a reason," but was understandably saddened by the situation.

"As a football player you know one day you'll have to hang up your cleats but you just hope it's on your own terms," he wrote. "It's hard to explain what it feels like to go through the highest of highs to the lowest of lows in the [ sic] matter of seconds."

Thompson was selected by Atlanta 208th overall in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Washington, where he spent his senior season after stints with Iowa and Western Michigan. On May 14, the Falcons announced that they had agreed to terms with Thompson and fellow rookie Avieon Terrell.

Two months later, on July 29, Atlanta officially placed Thompson on the NFI list, where he has remained since the start of the season.

Atlanta head coach Kevin Stefanski was asked about Thompson's status during a press conference on Friday, but the coach did not have any updates on the tackle's condition.

It is unclear if Thompson will choose to medically retire, but for now he will stay on the Falcons' roster as a reserve.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson, A.J. Brown, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 8
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson is officially back.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens quarterback, who hasn't played since Week 4, will be on the field for the Week 8 clash against Buffalo Bills.

That's a huge boost for fantasy football players who have spent the last few weeks piecing together their quarterback situations.

Elsewhere in the AFC, A.J. Brown is questionable to play in the New England Patriots' AFC East battle against the Miami Dolphins.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news that will affect Week 8's fantasy football matchups.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed on Friday that Lamar Jackson will return to the field on Sunday.

Jackson missed the last three weeks with an ankle injury. Baltimore went 1-2 in that stretch with Tyler Huntley at quarterback.

Jackson's return provides an immediate boost for Zay Flowers' fantasy football stock.

Rashod Bateman, Mark Andrews and the other Ravens pass-catchers are more intriguing waiver-wire options in Week 8 because of Jackson's presence.

The Ravens are going up against a Bills defense that conceded at least 340 yards in every one of its games. Two of Buffalo's last three opponents produced over 400 total yards.

The last two Ravens-Bills matchups produced 52 and 81 points. Another track meet could break out in Baltimore. That would be an ideal return for Jackson from a fantasy perspective.

He might not run as much as the ankle continues to heal, but the passing attack should achieve a good amount of success against the Bills.

A.J. Brown is questionable with ankle and knee ailments.

Brown missed the last two days of practice with his injuries.

That's not exactly a good sign for Brown's Sunday status. The Patriots will make a final decision this weekend on whether or not the veteran wide receiver will go in Miami.

Brown has been a disappointment so far in New England. He's had nine catches for 101 receiving yards in just three appearances.

Drake Maye's found a way to work around Brown's absences. He ranks eighth in the NFL in passing yards and he's tied for eighth in touchdown passes.

If Brown doesn't play, Hunter Henry and Demario Douglas should be the Patriots to target off the waiver wire.

Henry has 11 catches on 12 targets in the last two weeks. He's an ideal pickup at tight end with or without Brown.

Douglas would be New England's No. 1 wide receiver on Sunday without Brown. He'd be expected to break loose against a vulnerable Miami defense that let up over 240 passing yards in half of its games.

Washington's Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams are among the potential waiver-wire pickups for Week 8, if Brown doesn't play. The Commanders face a Philadelphia defense that gives up the second-most receiving yards to wide outs.

Dallas' Ryan Flournoy is an intriguing option as well. He faces an Arizona secondary that's allowed 10 touchdowns to wide receivers.

Omar Cooper Jr. of the New York Jets and Jacksonville's Jakobi Meyers are other waiver-wire pickups to consider given the roles they have in their respective passing attacks.

articles.title: New Patriots Rumors Update Christian Barmore's Availability at NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore is reportedly available as the Nov. 10 trade deadline nears, per Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated.
articles.body:
New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore is reportedly available as the Nov. 10 trade deadline nears, per Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated.

"The Patriots are deep in the AFC race, but veteran DT Christian Barmore could be had, having played only 41.9 percent of the team's defensive snaps, falling behind Milton Williams and Cory Durden in the team's rotation."

New England selected Barmore with a second round pick (No. 38 overall) in the 2021 NFL draft. He's played 71 games (28 starts) over five-plus seasons. Barmore's best season was 2023, when the former Alabama star amassed 8.5 sacks, 64 tackles (39 solo) and 16 quarterback hits.

In April 2024, Barmore signed a four-year, $84 million contract extension, per Over the Cap .

Unfortunately, Barmore was diagnosed with blood clots in July 2024, and he ultimately played just four games the following season.

He returned to the field in 2025 and became a full-time starter for the first time in his career. Over 17 games (16 starts), Barmore had 29 tackles, 11 quarterback hits and two sacks.

Barmore has been productive getting to the quarterback through six games (three sacks). Pats analyst Carlos A. Lopez spoke more on his pass-rushing skills.

However, Barmore has seen his playing time dip down from 65 percent of the defensive snaps in 2025, per Pro Football Reference . He has started just one of six games.

Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked about that in a recent press conference.

We'll see if Barmore sticks around with the Pats after the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but in the meantime, New England is visiting Miami to play the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

articles.title: Cowboys' Stephen Jones Addresses NFL Trade Deadline Approach After Joey Porter Jr. Move
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are still open to buying at the trade deadline following a 3-4 start to the 2026 campaign, executive Stephen Jones indicated in a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are still open to buying at the trade deadline following a 3-4 start to the 2026 campaign, executive Stephen Jones indicated in a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

Jones said the Cowboys would consider more defensive additions after acquiring cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this season.

"Certainly, I wouldn't say we're anywhere close to where we want to be in terms of pressure on the opposing team's quarterbacks. You can do that a lot of different ways... [like] player acquisition, which we're always taking a look at, which I think we've shown, just as we brought Porter in here," Jones said. "We're certainly not opposed to that, either, and we'd certainly look at it if it made sense."

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

When asked if he was put off by prices in a trade market that recently saw the Chicago Bears give up two first-round picks for Jeffery Simmons, Jones pointed toward the Cowboys' willingness to give up a first- and second-rounder in order to acquire Quinnen Williams from the New York Jets last fall.

"We feel like our hands around what value is in the market, and if the right situation's there, and we feel good about it, feel good about what the player can do for us, then we're certainly, as we've shown, not afraid to move on those instincts," Jones said.

The Cowboys currently hold just four picks in the 2027 draft, which would to mark the lowest single-draft total in franchise history, per Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram.

The team is also competing in an injury-weakened division in which the Cowboys sit alone in second behind the New York Giants (4-2-1) but ahead of the Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) and Washington Commanders (1-4-1).

The Cowboys will have faced two potential deadline sellers in the visiting Arizona Cardinals and host Indianapolis Colts by the trade deadline. The Eagles play the Commanders and Giants over the same stretch.

The results of those contests could impact how big of a swing Dallas is ultimately willing to take by the time the trade window closes Nov. 10.

articles.title: Daron Payne Injured, Latest NFL Rumors on Commanders DT's Status and Return Timeline Amid Foot Issue
articles.summary: Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne will "likely" head to injured reserve after suffering a "significant" foot injury during Friday's practice, per Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.
articles.body:
Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne will "likely" head to injured reserve after suffering a "significant" foot injury during Friday's practice, per Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.

Payne has played all nine of his NFL seasons with Washington, which selected the former Alabama star with the 13th overall pick in the 2018 NFL draft.

He's started six games this season and amassed 14 tackles (seven solo), five quarterback hits and one sack.

Payne has only missed three career games (one in 2019, two in 2025), and one was due to a suspension following an altercation with Detroit Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown last year. The other two absences were because of an ankle sprain (2019) and a back injury (2025).

So he's been a beacon of durability and reliability and a stalwart on the defensive line for quite some time.

Ultimately, this is a devastating loss for Washington. Grant Paulsen of 106.7 The Fan offered more insight into the impact of the injury.

This has already been a difficult year on the injury front for Washington. Of note, wide receiver Terry McLaurin (torn patellar tendon) is out for the year, as are linebacker Leo Chenal (fractured neck). Left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps in training camp and has been out all year . Quarterback Jayden Daniels missed two-and-a-half games with a dislocated elbow. Now Payne would be out for at least four games if he's placed on injured reserve.

In part because of injuries, Washington is off to a 1-4-1 start. The Commanders will hope to get back on the winning track on Sunday evening when they host the Philadelphia Eagles.

articles.title: Former Longhorns DB Michael Taaffe joins special company with Miami
articles.summary: Michael Taaffe is following in the footsteps of former Dolphins star Patrick Surtain. The former Longhorns is thriving with Miami.
articles.body:
Less than a season into his NFL career, former Longhorns legend Michael Taaffe is joining impressive company. Through seven games, the Austin native has two interceptions. He is the first Miami Dolphins player since Patrick Surtain in 1998 to record multiple interceptions in his first six games.

While Taaffe has a small sample size, being linked to Surtain is an impressive achievement. He finished his NFL career with 37 interceptions and 538 total tackles. During his time with the Dolphins, Surtain also made three Pro Bowls, a feat that Taaffe also hopes to achieve. If Taaffe can match Surtain's production, taking him in the fifth round will be a steal.

For those who have watched Taaffe's development, his stellar play comes as no surprise. During his time as a Longhorn, the former walk-on had 222 total tackles and seven interceptions. He also had 21 pass deflections and became a key piece of the defense.

Although his statistics were impressive, Taaffe also filled his trophy case. He earned multiple SEC honors and was named a s emifinalist for the 2024 Burlsworth Trophy. The Dolphins rookie also made 2025 preseason watch lists for the Bronko Nagurski Trophy, Jim Thorpe Award, and Lott IMPACT Trophy. That is partly why Miami didn't pass up the chance to add him to their secondary.

With the regular season far from over, Taaffe has plenty of time to solidify a spot for next season and show why he should be a key piece of the Dolphins' future.

articles.title: Ryan Poles says Bears aren't adopting 'F them picks' mindset with Jeffery Simmons trade, DT's impact on culture factored into deal
articles.summary: Chicago sent the Tennessee Titans 2027 and 2028 first-round picks, along with a 2027 fourth-round pick, in exchange for the 3-time All-Pro and a 2028 fifth-r...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears' trade for former Tennessee Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons came together quickly. But it had been brewing for a lot longer, general manager Ryan Poles explained on Friday.

Poles, now in his fifth season as GM, said that, over the past two years, the Bears had been discussing the three-time All-Pro and what adding him could mean for the franchise.

"I honestly didn't think it would ever happen," Poles admitted to reporters. "So when that window kind of opened where it was a possibility, and they had to work their process as well, it happened pretty fast.

"It was a late call and happened in the early morning."

The Bears sent the Titans 2027 and 2028 first-round picks on Thursday, along with a 2027 fourth-round pick, in exchange for the 29-year-old Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The transaction sent shockwaves through the NFL, igniting debates about whether the Bears overpaid or Simmons was worth the hefty price .

Simmons is the first DT in the common draft era — since 1967 — to be traded for multiple first-round picks, per ESPN . While expensive, it could just be the move that puts a 5-2 Chicago team with Super Bowl aspirations on the path to a Lombardi Trophy.

"The trade told me everything I needed to know, especially the value … from giving away two first-round picks," Simmons said Friday. "I could look on the other side of that and be like, 'Man, I just got traded,' but I can also look on the bright side of things of, 'This team believes in what they have here and they want it right now.'"

Poles clarified that the Simmons trade doesn't indicate a paradigm shift. More specifically, the Bears aren't adopting a front-office approach made famous by the Los Angeles Rams and their GM, Les Snead .

"I know it's kind of a joke that kind of goes around, but 'F them picks' is a big thing," Poles said. "That's really not what we're about. I know it took a lot to get this done, but we absolutely believe that the draft and bringing in young talent is a way that you sustain success around here."

Poles maintained that, in order to pull the trigger on a trade like the one that ushered Simmons to Chicago, he needs to be aiming for a player that makes a difference on the field and influences the organization's culture.

"I don't think it can be either or when you talk about a move this size," Poles said. "You need to have both. And that's what Jeffery does. We believe he's going to impact us at a high level on the grass but also in the locker room, too."

Simmons brings intensity, upholds standard of play Bears already preach

Simmons stands 6-foot-4, 305 pounds. His presence is imposing at the podium and even more daunting in between the white lines.

Last season, he piled up 11 sacks en route to first-team All-Pro honors. This time around, he's mounted four more, in addition to forcing a fumble and defending four passes. Through seven games, he's tied for third among all NFL interior defensive linemen with 24 pressures generated during the 2026 campaign, according to Pro Football Focus.

Simmons is what Poles describes as a "red-level interior defensive lineman." Every Super Bowl team in recent years has one, the GM asserted on Friday.

"I think he's a multiplier," Poles said, meaning that Simmons' effect up front helps not only the defensive line but also the other parts of the defense, namely the secondary. Just as the attention he draws in the middle of the trenches is expected to unlock the pass-rushing potential of his former Mississippi State teammate, Bears defensive end Montez Sweat, it's supposed to assuage the obstacles facing the defensive backs as well.

That prospect obviously made Simmons alluring. Yet so did the way he goes about his business and holds others accountable.

"His intensity that he brings to the football field, he has a certain standard of how you play this game," Poles said. "You've heard that from me, from [head coach] Ben [Johnson] throughout the years, and [Jeffery] lives that, he models that behavior.

"I think that when you don't live that, he's a guy that makes it a little bit uncomfortable for you, too, which is important. I don't know if we have that right now, and we do with adding him."

Simmons expressed that he's dedicated time to learning how to refine his leadership skills as his career has progressed. The 2019 No. 19 overall pick stressed the significance of figuring how to reach each individual player and calculating the right method for communicating the desired standard without coming off the wrong way.

He mentioned that Pro Football Hall of Famer DeMarcus Ware advised him to "give guys a vision and not an outcome."

Simmons will be keeping that in mind as he tries to elevate a defense coordinated by Dennis Allen that now should be able to get more pressure with its four-man rush.

At the moment, Simmons is still processing some of the emotions from this week's whirlwind, which saw him leave Nashville after seven-plus seasons. He's gearing up for what he said is his first primetime game since 2023.

Fittingly, he'll be facing longtime rival Quenton Nelson, a former Indianapolis Colts standout guard who just got traded to the Seattle Seahawks . They'll be once again going head-to-head, this time on Monday night in Seattle.

"I love competition, so there's nothing I don't like about Quenton Nelson," Simmons said. "I mean, he's a true competitor. He's a guy that's going to always bring his A game. When we play against each other, it's always a great matchup. I look forward to it every time I get ready to play against him."

He added: "I hated the Colts. That's what it was. I'm sure the Chicago Bears hate the Packers around here. So it's like, trust me, I'll get on board real soon with that."

Before he's even played a down for the Bears, his willingness to embrace and shape the organization's culture showed — it's among the chief reasons why Poles gave up so much to get him.

articles.title: Two former Sooners among PFF's highest-graded rookies this season
articles.summary: Two former Oklahoma Sooners standouts are off to fast rookie starts in the NFL.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners had seven players selected in the 2026 NFL Draft , and several are already playing key roles as rookies on their NFL clubs. However, a couple of former OU standouts have consistently performed well through the NFL's first seven weeks.

Pro Football Focus (PFF) and writer Gordon McGuinness released a list of their top 15 highest-graded rookies in the league so far this season , and two former Sooners made the cut. First was former linebacker Kendal Daniels, who now plays for the Atlanta Falcons. He checked in at No. 5, which is made all the more impressive by the fact that he suffered a scary-looking injury and came back to action last week.

"Daniels was phenomenal for the Atlanta Falcons in Sunday's win over the San Francisco 49ers, earning a 90.5 PFF grade. He recorded 10 solo tackles, three of which resulted in defensive stops, and came away with his first career interception." - Gordon McGuinness, PFF.

Daniels spent just one season in Norman, but he had immediate impact in 2025. He was a starter on OU's vaunted defense, and he was a perfect fit at the Cheetah position. His overall grade right now as a rookie is 77.7.

Also making the list was former defensive back Robert Spears-Jennings, who now plays for the Pittsburgh Steelers. He checked in at No. 7 on the list, quite the feat for a seventh-round pick.

"Spears-Jennings delivered another solid performance for the Steelers in Sunday's win over the Saints in Paris, earning a 76.5 PFF grade. He has yet to earn a PFF grade below 60.0 in a game during his young career and has missed just one of his 15 tackle attempts as a rookie." - McGuinness, PFF.

Spears-Jennings played for the Sooners for four years, developing into the leader of the OU secondary as a senior in 2025. He was one of the foundational players that helped Oklahoma build its defense in the early years of the Brent Venables era.

The Sooners had their most productive NFL draft in awhile this past year, and there are multiple players who are already making their mark at the next level.

articles.title: What we learned about new Chicago Bears DT Jeffery Simmons, a ‘terrifying guy to go against’
articles.summary: Jeffery Simmons had no idea how much his identity was about to change Thursday morning. He was the face of the Tennessee Titans franchise, at least on the de...
articles.body:
Jeffery Simmons had no idea how much his identity was about to change Thursday morning.

He was the face of the Tennessee Titans franchise, at least on the defensive side, when he entered their practice facility

"Went into the building, sitting down with teammates eating breakfast, got a phone call from my agent and of course he broke the news," Simmons told the Chicago media Friday at Halas Hall.

The news was seismic: The Bears swung a blockbuster trade to acquire Simmons for two first-round picks — one in next year's draft and the other in 2028 — as well as a 2027 fourth-round pick. The Bears also received a 2028 fifth-round draft pick.

He called the move a "blessing" but one that carried a lot of emotions. Simmons became a Titan — he became the Titan — when they drafted him with the 19th pick in 2019.

"I've tried everything I had into me to pour into the city of Nashville and to that organization," he said. "Things happen in this business."

But this one hit home on a personal level.

"You learn that and try to take the feelings out of it, but I tell you, yesterday was pretty hard to have that phone call with my family and to leave my daughter (Mulani)," Simmons said. "That was probably the hardest part yesterday, hugging her before I headed to the airport. Three years old, at that age, they don't really understand what's about to happen. From almost seeing her every day of the week to (we've) got to figure out that schedule now. It's been a lot of emotions the last couple days.

"But today felt great. It felt great to get on the practice field, move around with the guys. Being back with Montez (Sweat), that was my road dawg at Mississippi State. So I'm excited to be here, I'm excited to be a Chicago Bear."

No one was more eager to have Simmons at Halas Hall than defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, who likened the trade to an early Christmas present.

"Obviously excited about acquiring Jeffery Simmons," he said. "He's a hell of a football player, but as much as he is, the athlete and the skill set that he has. I'm just as intrigued in bringing another guy into the building who has tremendous football and personal character."

Allen will go about the slow business of integrating Simmons snap by snap and week by week, beginning with a still-to-be-determined number of snaps Monday night against the Seattle Seahawks.

"We will see what he can digest and how much he can take in in a short period of time," Allen said. "The fact that he is such a professional and really studies the game allows him to catch up pretty quickly."

Here are three things we learned about Simmons from Halas Hall on Friday.

Bears guard Jonah Jackson remembers playing against Simmons as a Detroit Lion in December 2020 and during the Bears' joint practice with the Titans this summer.

"He's a dynamic player," Jackson said. "He can play the run very well. He can pass rush incredibly well. … You have to know where he is at all times, and that's something that strikes some fear into opposing offensive lines. Like they do in Seattle, they've got Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy, all those guys, you've got to be aware of where they are at all times, just like Jeff Simmons."

Simmons immediately plugs into the interior next to fellow veteran Grady Jarrett and should continue to see double teams from opposing offensive lines.

"I think any time you have a guy that can be as disruptive as he can be on the interior of your defense, it frees some other guys up too," Allen said. "But listen, this will be a work in progress in terms of how the defense changes or what changes with what we do or how we do it as we get a chance to see what he can do within our scheme."

Eventually, Simmons, who is tied for fifth in sacks among defensive linemen with four, should juice up the overall defense , which has been improving steadily.

The Bears' 37.9% pressure rate ranks 12th, and their 19 sacks is tied for eighth, though they've been relying a lot on blitzes (fourth-ranked at 40.6%).

Nickel corner Kyler Gordon and defensive end Austin Booker are tied for the team lead in sacks with four. Dayo Odeyingbo, who is on injured reserve , has three, Sweat two and Jarrett none.

"It's like I told Grady today, like, if I'm getting in the double (team), I expect you to go win," Simmons said. "That's pretty much what it is. Same thing I told Tez. If the tackles could hang on me and you can't get off the ball and get a free sack, there's something wrong.

"That just is (the) first-day conversation I'm having with these guys."

Defensive tackle Kentavius Street already felt a kinship with Simmons as onetime college prospects who tore their ACLs shortly before their respective NFL drafts — Street in 2018 and Simmons in '19.

"Jeffery's been a beast his whole career," Street said. "And to have him on my team finally is dope. It's amazing. He's going to command the slide (from a second offensive lineman or a chipping running back), and so I think it's going to demand even more one-on-ones for the rest of us. So we all can eat."

General manager Ray Poles said Sweat "for sure" should be one of the linemates who eats, as Street put it.

"That's why I really believe that the closest path to the quarterback, to the ball, is inside, and oftentimes that will open up some things on the outside for your guys," Poles said. "Just talking with Montez, he's locked in, ready to go. This is one of his guys and I think he elevates his game, being around Jeffery.

"That's our expectation. I think that's the expectation he has for himself as well."

2. Simmons addressed the 'painted nails' comment.

Williams famously paints his fingernails in different colors, messages and themes.

In a macho sport, that has drawn attention, especially from a self-branded "smack talker" such as Simmons.

"Painted nails. I can't wait to say that to him," Simmons said on the "Rich Eisen Show" in July 2024, a few months before facing Williams in his NFL debut, a 24-17 Bears win.

But Simmons said it hasn't lingered as an issue. The two shook hands after a practice in Nashville, he said.

"Being a fan of Caleb, of course, being on the other side having to play against him, I'm not going to tell him that," Simmons said. "I'm going to talk as much smack as I can. But now he's on my team. We're teammates now. "I'll go to war for any of my guys in the locker room. I hope Caleb would know that."

Williams has seen his fair share of shots about his nails from all corners. But it's not often you come face-to-face with a peer who was so vocal about it.

"Those comments a couple of years ago about his nails and whatnot, it's all lips," Simmons said. "It's part of my game now with the smack talk. You guys heard that I'm probably one of the best smack talks. I talk a lot of smack when I'm on the field. I'm looking forward to being his teammate. We all know what type of player he is. I'm looking forward to helping him get the ball."

3. Just in time for Halloween, Press Taylor revisited a 'terrifying' story.

Offensive coordinator recalled hearing clapping at Halas Hall around noon Thursday, his first signal that the Bears acquired Simmons.

"And then I get a FaceTime from my brother (Cincinnati Bengals coach Zac Taylor), which we don't normally talk until like late in the week, with just a huge smile," he said. "And I'm like, 'Thank you. We're excited.' And he's like, 'No. We play the Titans this week.' Oh, so that makes a lot more sense for why you're excited."

Press Taylor held some no-so-fond memories of Simmons as the former offensive coordinator of the Jacksonville Jaguars.

"I was in the (AFC South) division for four years with the guy and I know it's a nightmare," he said. "Twice a year it was an absolute nightmare having to deal with him — just being aware of where he is, how you're blocking him every given play. And you know what he's going to do.

"He's a high-motor, incredibly productive, terrifying guy to go against. I'm glad we're not going against him anymore."

articles.title: Chiefs Linked to Buccaneers’ $66 Million Pro Bowler in Blockbuster Trade Proposal
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs have emerged as a possible landing spot for Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Chris Godwin in a trade proposal ahead of the NFL deadl...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs have emerged as a possible landing spot for Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Chris Godwin in a trade proposal ahead of the NFL deadline.

Godwin's dip in production following a 2024 ankle injury and his heavy contract have contributed to discussion about a possible move to an AFC contender.

Chiefs floated as surprise destination for Chris Godwin

Godwin signed a three-year, $66 million contract before the 2025 season. A serious injury ended his 2024 campaign. Since then, he has recorded 56 catches for 576 yards and two touchdowns across 15 games.

Fowler wrote , "Godwin is a legacy Buc through 10 seasons, but he hasn't been quite the same since his 2024 ankle injury. His veteran presence and savvy play could help another team. He's due $22 million in cash this year, which could be a deterrent to a deal, though."

His 2026 numbers have dropped further, with film analysis showing he has yet to top 50 receiving yards in a single game as his play speed declines. Those figures fall short of Tampa Bay's previous expectations.

Bleacher Report's Brad Gagnon ranked Godwin's deal among the NFL's worst contracts. Gagnon cited missed time, declining production, and high salary.

The Patriots once offered Godwin more than $90 million before 2025. He chose to stay in Tampa Bay despite that offer. Godwin averaged 10.3 yards per catch across 15 games in 2025. The decline shows how much his production has slipped.

Godwin's contract makes a trade difficult. His $33.7 million cap hit is the highest among wide receivers. Moving him would leave Tampa Bay with a major financial hit. However, Kansas City's need for veteran depth keeps the door open ahead of the deadline.

ESPN assesses Godwin's trade probability at 15 percent, with his massive contract presenting the primary hurdle for prospective buyers. But football analyst Matt Bowen reviewed his game tape and noted that Godwin remains a smart slot receiver. He can play in different positions and catch passes in crowded areas over the middle.

The Chiefs and Steelers are both looking for veteran receivers. League officials are also monitoring other top targets, such as Brian Thomas Jr. and Jerry Jeudy, before the November 10 deadline.
